### AUDIT_PATTERNS.md — P20 and P21 bodies, verbatim before compression to probe + standing-lesson form

The live entries keep both PROBES (P20: grep the LITERAL and classify by
representation; P21: open the authority and diff the accept-sets) and each
pattern's standing lesson, because the index's reason for keeping two numbers
is that the two probes differ. What moves here is the instance catalogue.

20. **A predicate keys on ONE SPELLING of a type whose grammar admits several, so semantically identical schemas take different code paths.** Avro spells one type more than one way — bare `"null"` and wrapped `{"type":"null"}` are the same branch (likewise `"int"`), and the wrapped form may carry props or a logicalType, both inert on a null. The spellings land in DIFFERENT fields (`aschema.primitive` vs `aschema.object`), so `x.primitive == "null"` silently means "bare only" while its twin `x.kind == "null"` sees both. Invisible to every round-trip and wire net (the two spellings produce IDENTICAL wire bytes — only derived artifacts diverge: ser/deser arm, `fieldMeta`, lift target, consume verdict, error identity) and to any matrix whose union fragments are all bare-spelled (spelling as the held-CONSTANT axis, B32). **Probe: grep the LITERAL, not the accessor** — `grep -n '== "null"'` over non-test files, then classify each hit by REPRESENTATION. An accessor sweep (`\.primitive ==\|\.kind ==\|\.Type ==`) sees only the parsed/compiled node and is structurally blind to the pre-Parse `any` tree, where a branch is an `[]any` ELEMENT (`union[0] == "null"`) with no field to name. The representations to enumerate: parsed `aschema` · compiled/metadata node kind (normalized) · pre-Parse `any` tree (SchemaFor composition, cache splice). **The standing lesson: one shared predicate per REPRESENTATION is the ceiling — a fix routed through a predicate reaches only the representations that call it, so a sweep must enumerate representations, not call sites.** Fixed 2026-07-25 in two rounds: `aschema.isNullBranch` for the parsed tree (5 call sites), then `isNullBranchTree` for the pre-Parse tree (SchemaFor's pointer collapse + null-first default fill, which the first round's accessor sweep could not see). Netted by `TestMatrix_NullBranchSpellingParity` (519 cells, parsed/compiled) + `TestMatrix_SchemaForNullBranchSpellingParity` (96 cells, pre-Parse) + `TestDifferentialFastavroSchemaForNullSpelling` (foreign readresolve over the EMITTED schema — the only oracle that sees a dropped `"default":null`, since twmb infers it and Java/fastavro do not). Instance narratives verbatim: archive (2026-07-25 #8).

21. **A consult-side guard hand-enumerates what an AUTHORITY accepts, instead of asking the authority.** Some rule already has one owner — a resolver (`scopedRefKeys`/`lookupNameRef` owns "which spellings bind to this name"), or the stdlib (`encoding/json`'s `resolveKeyName` owns "what does a map key emit"). A later guard that must answer the SAME question restates the rule as a hand-written list of accepted cases. The list is a snapshot: it is missing members from the day it is written, and it cannot track the authority. Two failure directions, both silent at review time because the restatement READS correct: **under-enumeration** rejects input the authority accepts (a guard that lists two spellings when the resolver binds three), and **missing guards** drops a defensive branch the authority has (a charge arm that calls `MarshalText` where the stdlib checks nil first, converting a valid value into a panic). The tell in review is prose of the form "the two forms X binds" / "mirrors X's resolver" beside a literal enumeration — that comment is a claim (convention 5), and the way to check it is to READ the authority and diff the sets, never to read the comment. Probe: for any predicate whose doc names another function as the rule's source, open that function, enumerate its accepted set / its guards, and cross every member against the predicate; then ask whether the predicate could have CALLED it instead (a one-entry table, a shared helper) — delegation is the fix, a longer literal list is the same bug with a later expiry. Pairs with B14 (the new helper a fix introduces is itself audit territory) and P19 (both are "the replacement is coarser/narrower than what it replaced").
    Instance (both 2026-07-25, both introduced by the fix generation quarantined the following round): `nodeRefTargetAgrees` (schema_node.go) gated the name-reference splice on "Type is the target's fullname or its short name — the two forms the reference resolver binds", but `scopedRefKeys` binds THREE (fullname · enclosing-namespace-qualified short name · the `.x` null-namespace escape) and matches against the RESOLVED fullname, not the target's `Name` field — so an unedited extracted sub-node whose reference used the dot escape, or whose definition wrote its name dotted (`{"name":"ns.Foo"}`) and was referenced short, stopped converting ("unknown primitive"). `mapKeyEmitLen` (schema_node.go) restated `encoding/json`'s key resolver to charge non-string keys but omitted its `k.Kind() == Pointer && k.IsNil()` guard, so a nil pointer key implementing `TextMarshaler` panicked inside the budget walk that exists to make hostile trees safe.

   Instance: the stray-body re-decode elimination recorded shape verdicts per canonical stray key (`strayShapeRecorded`: `o.Items != nil` for "items") and consulted them from `for k, v := range m` — `{"type":"int","items":"int","ITEMS":12}` consumed the malformed `ITEMS` body on the valid `items` verdict (vanished from Props on both surfaces, vs #63's Props-verbatim clause), and the metadata loop's non-recursive keys kept per-body checks while the parse loop didn't, splitting CustomType-callback props from Root().Props on `{"type":"int","name":"x","NAME":12}`. Resolved first by pick-gating every consult at all four routing sites; the whole picked-vs-variant distinction was then SUBSUMED by the #46 exact-case re-ruling (2026-07-21): reserved keys match exact-lowercase only, so the verdict is consulted for exactly the spelling the arms read and variants are plain props with no routing. The pattern's lesson stands independent of that fix's fate: any recorded/threaded verdict must be keyed at least as finely as the loop that consults it. Net: `TestMatrix_ReservedKeyDuplicateSpellings` + field/splice twins + `TestMatrix_ReservedKeyVariantOnly`; NOT_BUGS #46.

### NOT_BUGS.md #63 — the stray-structural-key family, verbatim before compression

The live entry keeps every clause LETTER with its ruling and its nets, so a
later round can still tell (a) from (j) and find the pin. What moves here is
the per-clause narrative: how each was found, what the blast-radius
measurement showed, which driver defect a neuter caught. Those are round
narratives, and the rounds that produced them are archived above
(2026-07-23 #4, 2026-07-27 #2, 2026-07-27 #3).

63. **(tombstone, fully netted) The stray-structural-key family (maintainer-adjudicated 2026-07-14; clauses through 2026-07-23).** (a) EXCLUSIVITY: a container kind carrying ANOTHER kind's defining key hard-rejects (`invalid <kind> has schema for other types`) — keep-strict; Java (props) and fastavro (executed accepts) diverge; the reject is the cache/metadata walkers' kind-keyed-child-scope soundness premise. (b) SHAPE-CONDITIONAL ROUTING on a kind that does not bind the key: a schema-shaped stray body surfaces structurally as-written as its ONLY surface (render dedup skips stray-reached names; survival is props-independent), and a malformed body rides in Props verbatim as its ONLY surface — structural field stays ZERO; capture⟺shape-verdict: the metadata captures run the parser's own decodes (`stringSliceFrom`/`decodeLaxInt`), so structural-field-set ⟺ parse-consumed. (c) A wrapped reference REJECTS schema-shaped structural keys ("unknown complex type"); non-structural/malformed extras merge onto the spliced def as props, def-wins exact-key (Java drops usage-site extras; fastavro rejects the spelling — executed). (d) SchemaFor's walkers pass unbound structural keys through untouched, verdict-parity with Parse. (e) The binding-kind gate is `walkNodeChildren`'s DEFAULT; only the metadata walker opts into stray enumeration (pinned asymmetry). (f) Exact-case only (#46): stray routing is placement-conditional, never case-conditional. (g) **BARE-EMISSION losslessness (fixed 2026-07-27):** clause (b)'s "surfaces structurally as-written as its ONLY surface" holds through `Root().Schema()`, which it previously did not. The metadata render collapses a node to its bare type name only when the node carries NOTHING beyond `Type` — asked once, as `nodeCarriesOnlyType` (schema_node.go), DERIVED from SchemaNode's field set. Before, the two sites that ask it (the primitive arm and the name-reference arm of `toJSONWalk`) each held their OWN hand-written list of remembered fields, and both lists were missing the same members: a schema-shaped stray `symbols`, `size`, `aliases`, `doc` or `name` on a primitive survived `String()` and `Root()` and was SILENTLY DROPPED by the rebuild, while a stray `name` was caught by one list only. Blast radius MEASURED across five surfaces × 15 shapes: exactly the rebuild column changed; canonical form, `String()`, and wire bytes are byte-identical. `Branches` is the ONE classified exemption — no JSON key routes to it outside a union, so a hand-built value on another kind is inert and cannot be lost (pinned by `TestRegression_NonUnionBranchesInertInRebuild`). The durable guard is not the fix but `TestInvariant_BareEmissionCoversEverySchemaNodeField`, which sets every exported field in turn and requires the predicate to notice, so a field added later FAILS until someone classifies it — the enumeration checks itself instead of trusting the next author. Census Q16 drives the two asking sites, with its MEMBERS classified rather than counted. **(h) Losslessness is a CONJUNCTION, and clause (g) proved only half of it (2026-07-27).** A completeness guard that requires the shortcut to BLOCK on a populated field says nothing about whether the longer form it falls through to actually EMITS that field, so a value could still be dropped with nothing but the render changed — which `EnumDefault` did: it blocked, the emitter keyed `"default"` off `HasEnumDefault`, and `(&SchemaNode{Type:"int",EnumDefault:"S1"}).Schema()` emitted `{"type":"int"}`. The guard is now a ROUND TRIP — set, emit, re-parse, and read the value back off the metadata FIELDS (never the rendered text, whose key ORDER made an earlier survival check report losses that had not happened) — and every exported field carries one of three classifications, each checked in both directions: EXEMPT (`Branches` off a union, `EnumDefault` without its carrier: no emitted form, so it must NOT block), RELOCATED (`Precision`/`Scale`: the emitted key rides to Props on a carrier that does not bind it, #71), or ROUND-TRIPPING on its own field (the other 11). `HasEnumDefault` was originally a FOURTH classification — it blocked, emitted, and was then DROPPED, because `"default"` was reserved on every kind while only an enum had a field to capture it into. Clause (j) closed that class: it is now RELOCATED like `Precision`/`Scale`, and the guard carries only three classifications, so a field that emits a key the re-parse discards fails there instead of being classified as an accepted loss. **(i) The SIBLING predicate on the same walk (2026-07-27).** `nodeIsNameRefShape` — whether a stamped reference may be replaced by the definition it names — was the other hand-written list, of eight fields, and it SILENTLY DISCARDED the seven it did not name (`LogicalType`, `Namespace`, `Aliases`, `Doc`, `EnumDefault`, `Precision`, `Scale`) on an extracted-then-EDITED node. It is now derived through the same walk, `nodeCarriesNothingBut`, with an exemption set that is EXACTLY the adjudicated usage-site attributes: `Doc`/`Aliases`/`Namespace`/`LogicalType` per #25 (a definition cannot carry a second name, namespace or doc for its usage site — and the parse LANDS those four on the structural fields, so deriving without them would convert #25's adjudicated silent drop into a hard "unknown complex type" error on the extraction feature), plus `Props`, which clause (c) MERGES. `Precision`/`Scale` are deliberately NOT exempt even though they are usage-site attributes too: the parse routes an unconsumed pair to Props, so a non-zero value on those FIELDS can only be a caller's direct write. Three cells flip silent→loud (`EnumDefault`, `Precision`, `Scale`); the whole-schema path is untouched, and the full suite was green through the flip, which is itself the measurement that no test covered them. Registered as census **Q17**, whose driver runs the metadata splice and the CACHE splice over one corpus and requires the same verdict per wrapper key, with the expectation taken from the rulings rather than from either implementation. Nets: `TestInvariant_BareEmissionCoversEverySchemaNodeField`, `TestInvariant_NameRefSpliceCoversEverySchemaNodeField`, `TestInvariant_NodeFieldRuleTablesNameRealFields` (the exemption SET is pinned, so widening it is a visible policy change), and `TestMatrix_CallerComposedAndEditedNodes` — 204 cells crossing {hand-built, extracted-unedited, extracted-edited} × every exported field × {Schema, String, Canonical, Fingerprint, JSON} over second-occurrence, forward-reference, RECURSIVE, DIAMOND and cache-cross-parse structures, asserting a value or a named error and never a panic. Each structure asserts its own precondition that the picked node IS a stamped bare reference, because the cache inlines its first occurrence and a pick that lands on the definition never reaches the splice at all. **(j) A reserved key that is neither BOUND nor SURFACEABLE has Props as its only surface — the type-level `default` and `order` (maintainer-RULED 2026-07-27, reversing the drop clause (h) recorded as policy).** Both are FIELD attributes. At the type level only an enum binds `"default"` (the evolution default, #54) and NO kind binds `"order"`, and neither has a SchemaNode field of its own on a kind that does not bind it — so under the old routing both were captured by the reserved-key set and then dropped, reaching neither a structural field nor Props. That violates the biconditional the whole family drives (structural field set IFF consumed, Props = raw keys minus consumed, never both and never neither) and it is the same class as clause (g)'s bare-emission loss: an as-written attribute that dies in `Root().Schema()` while (b) says as-written is its ONLY surface. Both references PRESERVE them where the kind does not bind: Java's `SCHEMA_RESERVED` (Schema.java:175-176) omits BOTH keys and `ENUM_RESERVED` (:178-180) adds `default` alone, applied at :1857/:1880/:1940/:1950/:1963 versus :1928 for enum, so `parsePropertiesAndLogicalType` keeps each as a schema property everywhere else; fastavro 1.12.2 keeps both on the parsed schema of every kind (EXECUTED, 28 differential cells). Cross-impl rule 2 points the same way, and this is PRESERVATION, not an accept/reject loosening. **#46 does not reach these cells and this is a REFINEMENT of it, not a reversal:** #46 governs CASE VARIANTS and presumes the exact spelling is CONSUMED ("exact+variant both present → exact consumed, variant a prop"); where the kind does not bind the key there is no capture, so the premise is absent. A case-variant `"Default"`/`"Order"` remains an ordinary prop under #46 exactly as before, on every kind including the one whose exact spelling binds. **SCOPE is type-level only:** Java's `FIELD_RESERVED` (:503-504 — `default, doc, name, order, type, aliases`) binds both at the FIELD level and so does twmb, so a record field's `default`/`order` stay consumed into `SchemaField.Default`/`.Order` and must never reach `SchemaField.Props` — pinned as the boundary by `TestRegression_FieldLevelDefaultOrderStayConsumed` and by the field arm of the matrix, and neuter-verified disjoint from the type arm. The routing is now DERIVED rather than enumerated: `schemaReservedKeyForObject` asks `schemaKeyBinds` and keeps a key out of Props for exactly two reasons — the kind BINDS it, or the kind SURFACES it as-written on a structural field (`canonicalStrayKey` plus a shape-OK body). An enumeration of consumed keys is a subset and a subset can be missing a member, which is precisely how these two fell through. Blast radius MEASURED over 77 shapes × 7 surfaces: the Parsing Canonical Form, the Rabin fingerprint, the binary wire and the Avro-JSON encoding are BYTE-IDENTICAL (both sides confirmed non-empty), and every field-level row is identical on every column; what changes is the metadata tree, the rebuild, the CustomType callback's `Props`, and one cache-splice `String()` where a wrapper `order` now merges onto the spliced definition as the ordinary custom property it became. Consumed-ness still wins at a splice: an enum definition swallows a wrapper's `"default"` rather than carrying a second one. Nets: `TestMatrix_TypeLevelBindingRouting` ({default, order} × 14 kinds × {type, field} × {Schema, String, Canonical, Fingerprint, JSON, wire}, with the attribute-free twin per cell), `TestRegression_TypeLevelDefaultOrderSurviveTheRebuild` (primitive, array, enum-that-binds-only-default, RECURSIVE definition, DIAMOND reference), `TestRegression_FieldLevelDefaultOrderStayConsumed`, the flipped census/Q4/Q17 cells, and `TestDifferentialFastavroTypeLevelBindingRouting` (preservation, not mere acceptance). Nets: the 360-cell stray-key matrix + `TestMatrix_StrayBodyShapeRouting` (wedge bodies; structural-zero on every malformed cell) + the strayPS placement × kind × {type,field,union-field} × body matrices + `TestMatrix_SpliceWrapperReservedKeyMerge` + the FEATURE × WALKER harness rows; fastavro arms executed. Re-opens: a new walker/consult of either tree representation without its R1 row, or a new reserved-key read/shape check not shared with the parser's decodes. Verbatim: BUG_AUDIT.md §Distillation archive (2026-07-23 #4).

### NOT_BUGS.md #71 and #54, verbatim before compression (same TRIPLE-distillation pass; the live entries keep every ruling, discriminator and pin — what moves here is the derivation narrative)

54. **Enum FIELD-default symbol membership is validated at schema parse — deliberately stricter than every reference; keep-strict (maintainer-adjudicated).** Java's parse-time field-default validation accepts ANY textual value for an enum-typed field default: `isValidDefault` groups ENUM with STRING/BYTES/FIXED and checks only `isTextual()` (Schema.java:1755-1759); symbol containment is enforced only for the enum-LEVEL `"default"` attribute in EnumSchema's constructor (Schema.java:1100). fastavro 1.12.2 parses a non-member enum field default outright (executed observation, claims-sweep round). twmb validates membership at parse because a non-member field default can never encode — accepting it just moves the failure from parse (fail-fast, actionable) to first default-fill encode (far from the schema author). The same check is what lets union default coercion pick a later branch instead of mis-selecting the enum on a non-member string (`TestRegression_UnionDefaultMetadataMatchesWireBranch_EnumArm`, conformance_test.go — the cross-impl paragraph there is the executed record). Do NOT re-file "Java/fastavro accept a non-member enum field default" as an interop divergence: cross-impl rule 1 (a default that can never encode is a latent failure, not data) decided keep-strict.
    **Enum-LEVEL non-string/null defaults (overseer-adjudicated 2026-07-14 extension): twmb's reject is fastavro-CORROBORATED, not twmb-stricter.** `{"type":"enum","name":"E","symbols":["A","B"],"default":3}` and `"default":null` both reject: twmb with `enum default "" is not a member of symbols` (executed 2026-07-14 — the `""` echo is the ignored json.Unmarshal error of a non-string value, cosmetic only), fastavro 1.12.2 with `Default value for enum must be in symbols list` (executed 2026-07-14, both shapes). Only Java ignores them: its parser reads the enum-level default via `getOptionalText`, which returns null for non-text JSON, so the EnumSchema containment check is skipped and the malformed default silently drops. Two-of-three reject; the Java-only silent drop is the same anti-silent-drop shape as #55. Do NOT re-file "Java parses enum defaults twmb rejects" for non-string/null enum-level defaults.

    **Closing clause (overseer-adjudicated 2026-07-24): the reject is decided by TOKEN TYPE, not by membership-on-the-Unmarshal-zero-value — the "cosmetic only" call above was wrong about the mechanism.** The old membership-only check let the ignored `json.Unmarshal` error's `""` (and null's no-error no-op) flow into the symbol test, so under a `WithLaxNames` fn accepting empty name components a schema whose symbols legitimately include `""` ACCEPTED `"default":5`/`null` and silently BOUND the `""` symbol — resolution filled it for unknown writer symbols while `Root().HasEnumDefault` reported false (wire↔metadata split). Post-fix (schema.go enum build): a non-string token — number, bool, array, object, explicit null — hard-rejects `enum default <token> is not a string` (bounded echo naming the token, which also fixed the cosmetic `""` echo) in BOTH strict and lax modes, BEFORE membership; an explicit `"default":""` stays legal exactly when `""` is a member. Neither reference ever binds a non-string default: fastavro rejects (executed, above), Java binds none (Schema.java:1921-1925 `textValue()` → null skips the :1100 containment check). Consumer grid: R1-Q9. Pins: `TestRegression_EnumDefaultLaxPhantomBindRejected` / `_ExplicitNullRejected` / `_NonStringEchoNamesToken`, boundary `TestEnumDefaultEmptySymbolBoundary`, matrix `TestMatrix_EnumDefaultTokenClassElimination` (+ field-level `TestMatrix_EnumFieldDefaultTokenTypes`; wrapper-ref inertness `TestRegression_EnumRefWrapperDefaultInert`), differential `TestDifferentialFastavroEnumDefaultToken` (calibrated: fastavro TYPE-checks field defaults but not membership; rejects the wrapped-ref shape outright).

71. **Field-level "precision"/"scale" are consumed-conditional: unconsumed placements are inert custom properties whatever the value's JSON shape; consumed placements shape-reject loudly (maintainer-ruled 2026-07-23, cross-impl rules 1+2).** UNCONSUMED — no field logicalType, a non-"decimal" field logicalType, or "decimal" whose lift target is not a bytes/fixed carrier as-written (a named reference is not a carrier spelling, and the target's own logical annotation does not change where the lift points) — the pair rides to `SchemaField.Props` verbatim on every surface (parse-render as-written, `Root()`, the rebuild; the wire lift moves only shape-valid ints), exactly like a valid-int unconsumed pair: `afieldFromAny` records per-key shape verdicts and decides AFTER the type parses, because consumed-ness is unknowable at the arms. Java never validates the pair at field level (FIELD_RESERVED = {default, doc, name, order, type, aliases}, Schema.java:503-504; parseProperties Schema.java:1905); fastavro 1.12.2 accepts + preserves verbatim (executed, including the consumed-decimal malformed case — fastavro has no field lift). CONSUMED — the pair is consumed exactly where the lift's annotation LANDS on a decimal carrier: the target's EFFECTIVE logical (its own when it has one — closer-to-the-type wins — otherwise the field's) is "decimal" AND the target kind is bytes/fixed. The target is the primitive, the first non-null union branch, or the type object. There the malformed body keeps the LOUD reject, fired from the recorded shape error and naming the key. **Navigation/landing clause (re-ruled 2026-07-26 on executed wire evidence; supersedes the earlier "annotation-independent" wording, which was true of NAVIGATION — which target the lift addresses — and was wrongly applied to LANDING — whether the decimal actually applies).** A field-level "decimal" whose target already carries its own logical never lands, so its precision/scale annotate nothing and are INERT, riding to `SchemaField.Props` verbatim like any custom property. Proven on the wire, not asserted: `{"type":"bytes","logicalType":"big-decimal"}` under a field decimal(4,2) encodes `06027b04` — byte-identical with scale 0, with scale 2, and with no field-level logical at all. The DISCRIMINATOR that keeps this from loosening into "any annotation of its own is inert": when the target's own logical IS "decimal" the same parameters DO land, and scale 0 vs 2 diverges (scale 0 refuses 123/100 as unrepresentable without rounding) — those cells keep rejecting. #55 is untouched: it governs valid decimal placements, and this moves only cells whose effective logical is not decimal. Enforcement is structural — `liftTarget` is the ONE navigation and `liftEffectiveLogical` the one landing question, so `liftFieldLogicalIntoType` (which moves) and `fieldDecimalLiftConsumesPrecisionScale` (which judges) cannot address different types; census Q5 drives them against each other. Pins: `TestRegression_FieldDecimalNotLandingIsInert` (Props + wire identity + the discriminator) and the own-logical-is-decimal cells in `TestRegression_FieldDecimalConsumedMalformedParamReject`; the former `union-annotated-carrier-precision` cell pinned the pre-ruling behavior and was retired. Malformed-as-absent is forbidden: scale is OPTIONAL (spec default 0), so a malformed scale beside a valid precision would silently parse as decimal(p,0) — a silent wire-semantics change (#55 anti-silent-drop; the never-reject neuter reds exactly the scale-guard cell). FLAT (goavro-style) fields defer entirely to the TYPE-level gate — the pair routes into the lifted type object, so the flat verdict equals the nested twin's on every body shape (#56). Recorded divergence: fastavro validates decimal params on ANY type-level logicalType-"decimal" object (non-carriers included), rejecting non-numeric shapes; Java drops the logical on non-carriers via LogicalTypes.fromSchemaIgnoreInvalid (LogicalTypes.java:120; called Schema.java:1979) without reading the params — twmb follows Java, and the divergence is pinned by DIRECTION in the fastavro arm. **Spelling-agnostic clause (2026-07-25):** the union arm's "first non-null branch" scan — which decides WHICH branch the decimal lift targets, and therefore whether the pair is consumed at all — skips the null branch in either spelling the grammar admits, via the shared `aschema.isNullBranch`. A wrapped `{"type":"null"}` branch (with or without props or a logicalType, both inert on a null) is skipped exactly like the bare `"null"`, mirroring #33's clause; before it, a wrapped null was mistaken for the first NON-null branch, so the consume verdict flipped with the spelling and a `*big.Rat` no longer encoded. Pinned by `TestRegression_FieldDecimalLiftNullBranchSpellingAgnostic` and the spelling axis of `TestMatrix_NullBranchSpellingParity`. Nets: `TestRegression_FieldPrecisionScaleMalformedUnconsumedInert` / `TestRegression_FlatFieldMalformedPrecisionMatchesNestedTwin` / `TestRegression_FieldDecimalConsumedMalformedParamReject` / `TestRegression_FieldPrecisionValidUnconsumedSurfacesInProps` / `TestRegression_StrayFieldsElementPrecisionRouting`; the strayPS placement × kind × {type, field, union-field} × body matrix with its fastavro arm executed per accepted cell; `TestMatrix_SpliceWrapperReservedKeyMerge` + `TestRegression_SpliceDefFieldMalformedPrecisionRidesThrough`; five neuters, each red exactly its own cells.

### NOT_BUGS.md #33, verbatim before compression (same pass). Its unsupported-shapes list still named the object-form null branch, which the entry's OWN 2026-07-25 spelling-agnostic clause had made supported — kept here so the stale sentence is recoverable and the correction is auditable.

33. **Field-level `logicalType` annotation on unions is lifted onto the first non-null branch.** Schemas like `{"name":"ts","type":["null","long"],"logicalType":"timestamp-millis"}` (AVRO-2015/AVRO-3014 common user error) parse with `timestamp-millis` applied to the `long` branch, so encode/decode of `time.Time` work directly. Apache Avro detects + warns but doesn't lift (`Schema.java:1871-1877`); fastavro/hamba/goavro preserve it as a field property only. Twmb-unique among Go impls; wire identical (raw long varint). Edge `["null","string","long"]`+`timestamp-millis`: lift targets `string`, `validateLogical` detects mismatch, soft-drop (`o.Logical = ""`) clears — matches references (no logical effective). Metadata API does NOT reflect the lift (`Root().Fields[0].Type.LogicalType` empty; surfaces in `Field.Props["logicalType"]`) — matching all references. **Spelling-agnostic clause (2026-07-25):** "first non-null branch" means the first branch that is not the null TYPE, in either spelling the grammar admits — the bare `"null"` and the wrapped `{"type":"null"}` (with or without props / a logicalType, which are inert on a null) are the same branch. The skip previously matched only the bare form, so under `[{"type":"null"},"long"]` the annotation landed ON the null branch and a `time.Time` no longer encoded at all. Every as-written null-branch decision now routes through the one `aschema.isNullBranch` predicate. **Parameters-fill clause (ruled 2026-07-26; new policy — the arms' asymmetry was never adjudicated).** The ANNOTATION and its PARAMETERS are separate questions. Closer-to-the-type wins the ANNOTATION: a target already declaring its own `logicalType` keeps it and the field's is dropped. The field still completes MISSING precision/scale, but only where the EFFECTIVE logical (the target's own if it has one, else the field's) is `"decimal"` — routed through `liftEffectiveLogical`, the same predicate the consume verdict reads, so navigation, landing, and parameter completion cannot disagree. Before this, the object arm completed parameters and the union arm did not, so `{"type":"bytes","logicalType":"decimal"}` under a field carrying `precision`/`scale` BUILT while its `["null",{same}]` twin REJECTED `invalid union: decimal logical type requires precision` — the same post-lift schema, a spelling-dependent verdict. Basis: no reference has an opinion (Java warns and ignores the field-level form, fastavro preserves it as props), so this is twmb's own concession and INTERNAL CONSISTENCY governs, with cross-impl rule 2 breaking the tie toward accepting. The gate's side effect — parameters no longer copied onto a target whose effective logical is NOT decimal — is unobservable, MEASURED not assumed: canonical form (the transform strips them) and wire bytes are identical with the pair present, absent, and at scale 0 vs 2, because nothing but the decimal codec reads them. See `liftFieldLogicalIntoType` / `liftTarget` / `liftEffectiveLogical` in schema.go; pinned by `TestRegression_FieldLogicalLiftSpellingParity` (four spellings, identical verdict and wire), `TestRegression_FieldParamsOnNonDecimalTargetAreUnobservable`, and census Q5's now-measurable union cell. Landing rules for the consume verdict: #71's navigation/landing clause.

   The lift is a per-problem-shape concession, NOT "make every buggy schema work." Supported shapes (string-form `["null","T"]`, primitive-form `"T"`, single-object `{"type":"T"}`, each with field-level logical and no own annotation) were each added for a specific deployed-buggy/interop need. Other spec-equivalent shapes (object-form null `[{"type":"null"},"T"]`, `[{"type":"null"},{"type":"null"},"T"]`, lift onto non-first non-null branch) are INTENTIONALLY NOT supported. Auditors: do not file "spec-equivalent variants of supported shapes are unsupported" as findings. The bar for adding a shape is a real-world producer breakage — surface as Suspected with evidence and ask, do not unilaterally extend.

### NOT_BUGS.md #44, the fixed-SIZE-fold paragraph, verbatim before compression (same pass)

   **Fixed SIZE is folded INTO the union match predicate (kindsMatchTier), per spec + fastavro.** The spec's union-resolution match predicate is "both schemas are fixed whose sizes and (unqualified) names match" and selection takes "the first schema in the reader's union that matches" (`_index.md` lines 691, 717) — so size is part of MATCHING, not a post-selection check. `kindsMatchTier` returns `matchNone` for a same-name `fixed` whose `size` differs, so `findMatchingBranch` skips it and continues to a later size-matching branch: `Resolve(fixed F size 4, ["null", fixed F size 8, fixed F size 4])` decodes via the size-4 branch on both wires, order-independently, for Resolve AND CheckCompatibility. fastavro does the same (`match_schemas` returns `None` for a fixed size mismatch, `read_union` skips-and-continues — `_read_py.py`). Java does NOT skip-and-continue (`Resolver.firstMatchingBranch` returns on a full-name match then fails on size — `Resolver.java`, the 1.8.x soft-match whose own comment admits the spec-divergence), so Java errors; twmb previously shared Java's spec-violation and now follows the spec + fastavro per the Cross-implementation divergence policy (rules 2+3: relaxed, safe — a reorder-decodable value, no corruption). The direct (non-union) fixed path still validates size via `checkSameKind` / `doResolve`. Pinned by `TestRegression_UnionFixedSizeFoldedIntoSelection`. Probed against the spec, Java (`Resolver.java`), and fastavro 1.12.2 (source + execution).

### NOT_BUGS.md #49, verbatim before compression (same pass)

49. **Decimal VALUE-precision — the unscaled magnitude's digit count vs the schema's declared `precision` — is enforced on ENCODE only, never on DECODE. So a decimal whose unscaled value EXCEEDS `precision` but still FITS the fixed/bytes byte container (e.g. a `fixed(4)`+`decimal(precision=9,scale=2)` wire of `41 41 41 41` = unscaled `1094795585`, a 10-digit value ≥ 10^9) decodes to a `*big.Rat` on BOTH the binary and JSON paths, but RE-ENCODING that same value is rejected with "decimal value has N digits, exceeds schema precision P". This decode-accepts/encode-rejects asymmetry is faithful Java parity, not a round-trip bug.** twmb's encode side rejects via `checkDecimalPrecision` (ser.go, through `decimalUnscaledBytes`); the decode side builds the `*big.Rat` straight from the bytes (`setDecimalValue` / the `deser*Decimal` arms and their JSON twins) with NO precision check — verified consistent across binary decode, JSON decode, and encode. This mirrors Apache Avro (Java) EXACTLY: `Conversions.DecimalConversion.toBytes`/`toFixed` call `validate()`, which throws `AvroTypeException("Cannot encode decimal with precision X as max precision Y")` (`lang/java/avro/.../Conversions.java:115-170`), while `fromBytes`/`fromFixed` just do `new BigDecimal(new BigInteger(bytes), scale)` with no validation (`Conversions.java:105-124`). A `fixed(N)`/`bytes` container holds unscaled values in `[10^precision, 2^(8N-1))` that exceed the declared precision; decoding such a (foreign or hand-built) wire is permissive and lossless, re-encoding it is strict — same as Java. The same asymmetry means a schema's own `decimal` DEFAULT whose stored codepoint bytes exceed `precision` parses and auto-fills RAW (validated against the underlying fixed/bytes type — Java validates defaults against the underlying type too, not the logical precision), yet would be rejected if handed back as a structured `*big.Rat`. Do NOT "fix" by adding a decode-side precision reject (it would reject valid foreign wire Java accepts — cross-impl rule 2, lean permissive) NOR by relaxing the encode-side check (it matches Java's `validate()`). The combinatorial matrix round-trips only IN-precision decimals, so this boundary is otherwise unpinned. Distinct from #15 (which covers how precision is COUNTED — magnitude vs significand); this covers WHERE it is checked (encode only).

### NOT_BUGS.md #61, verbatim before compression (same pass)

61. **A contract-violating `encoding.TextAppender` is guarded only where its misbehavior is detectable: binary encode rejects a shorter-than-input return with a named error; everything else is documented trust (maintainer-adjudicated: minimal guard).** `appendAvroString`'s inline-write slow path reserves a 1-byte length placeholder, lets the user's `AppendText(dst)` write directly into the buffer, and backfills the real header from the returned slice's length — so the returned slice is trusted arithmetic input. The guard (`len(dst) < mark+hdrLen` → `SemanticError`, "AppendText returned a slice shorter than its input") converts the previously-panicking shape (a fresh short return like `return []byte(s), nil` — pre-guard: slice-bounds panic through `Schema.Encode` at every position where accumulated output exceeds the return; silent empty string at top level where the length information does not exist) into a named error. The residuals are DELIBERATE: (a) a fresh return >= the input length passes the length check and silently replaces all previously-encoded output (err == nil, typically an undecodable wire) — detecting it would cost a per-string memcmp of everything encoded so far, a hot-path tax rejected for the caller's own contract violation; (b) the JSON encoder materializes text via `AppendText(nil)` (`textValue`), so fresh returns are simply taken as the text verbatim — nothing to guard, and for violating appenders the two wire formats legitimately differ (binary rejects the short shape, JSON emits `"x"`). Reference posture EXECUTED (go1.26.2, GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2): Go's own `encoding/json/v2` panics IDENTICALLY on the same violating appender (`runtime error: slice bounds out of range [33:1]` in `jsontext.(*encoderState).AppendRaw`, which appends `'"'`, calls `appendFn(b)`, and slices `b[pos+1:len(b)-1]` from the returned slice) — the trusting posture is the stdlib norm; twmb's guard is strictly more defensive than the newest stdlib encoder, not less. json v1 never calls `AppendText` (MarshalText-only, materializing — immune); decode-side `TextUnmarshaler` receives bytes and returns only an error (immune). Do NOT extend the guard to prefix-compare, and do NOT re-file the silent shapes or the binary↔JSON violator divergence as bugs. Pinned by `TestRegression_AppendTextShortReturnNamedError` and `TestMatrix_AppendTextReturnShapes` / `TestMatrix_AppendTextReturnShapesJSONImmunity` (return shape × position, exact observed bytes for the undetectable shapes, plain-string-twin byte identity for legal appends; neuter-verified — disabling the guard reproduces the recovered panics at record/struct/array/map positions, the silent `x`-wire at union, and the pin's `[11:1]` panic, while every legal/silent/JSON cell stays green).

### NOT_BUGS.md #56, verbatim before compression (same pass)

56. **Flat-format (goavro-style) fields surface POST-LIFT in the metadata API (maintainer-adjudicated).** A field written as a bare string complex-kind type with the kind's defining key alongside the field's own keys (`{"name":"E","type":"enum","symbols":[...]}`) is a deliberate parse-input concession to linkedin/goavro's flat field format; the wire parser lifts the defining keys into a nested type definition named after the field (`liftFlatFieldType`, schema_parse.go). `Root()` describes that same post-lift schema: the type node carries the name and defining content, the routed keys (defining key, doc, logicalType/precision/scale, custom props; name/namespace for named kinds) do NOT appear in `SchemaField.Props`, and `Root().Schema()` rebuilds the nested form. Rationale: the as-written flat shape is unrepresentable through the rebuild — `toJSONWalk` emits a SchemaNode as a nested type OBJECT, and the lift gate fires only on a bare STRING type, so a Props-carrying posture cannot round-trip; and no reference posture exists because the references reject the flat form outright — fastavro 1.12.2 raises `UnknownType: enum/array/fixed` (executed observation, this round), and Java's parser resolves a textual field type as a NAME (`Schema.java:1828-1829`, `isTextual() → context.find(...)`; the complex-kind dispatch at :1830-1844 applies only to object nodes), so `"enum"` is an undefined name there. This is deliberately DIFFERENT from #33's field-level logicalType posture (Props-carrying, metadata does NOT reflect the lift): the logicalType lift's as-written shape — a primitive string type plus a field-level key — IS preserved by the rebuild and re-lifts on re-parse, so Props-carrying round-trips there; #33 is unchanged. The lift decision and key routing are shared helpers (`flatFieldNeedsLift` / `flatLiftTypeMap`, schema_parse.go) used by both the wire parser and the metadata walker, so the two sides cannot drift. Pinned by `TestRegression_FlatFieldRootSchemaRoundTrip`, `TestRegression_FlatFixedNameRefDefaultCoerced`, and the `TestMatrix_FlatFieldLift*` suite (kind × namespace × logicals × name-ref-default shapes × no-lift boundary parity × degenerate content; neuter-verified — gating the metadata twin off reproduces the empty-node / rebuild-error / uncoerced-default shapes on every lift-dependent cell while the no-lift parity cells stay green). Verdict parity (2026-07-23, #71): malformed precision/scale in the flat spelling take the TYPE-level consumed gate's verdict — the pair routes into the lifted type object — so flat and nested twins agree on every body shape (`TestRegression_FlatFieldMalformedPrecisionMatchesNestedTwin`).

Primitive objects keep accepting a stray `name` (childless: no child positions for that arm to act on). ### AUDIT_PATTERNS.md B20 (error-echo amplification), verbatim before compression (2026-07-27 #4; the live entry keeps the helper table, the sweep playbook and both sub-pattern greps)
- **Error messages echo unbounded user-controllable input — log / RPC / metric-label amplification.** Distinct from pattern 9 (parser-CPU) and pattern 16 (precision-fix DoS): the parser rejects in O(1) via a length cap, BUT the rejection message interpolates the input verbatim via `fmt.Errorf("…%q…", userInput)`. A 10 MiB hostile JSON.Number → 10 MiB error message → 1:1 amplification through logging, RPC error channels, Prometheus labels, tracing. The CPU posture is fine; the *string* posture is the DoS. Invisible to timing DoS probes (~0.1 ms), wire-correctness probes (error is correct, just enormous), and pre-existing unit tests (short hostile input, assert existence not size). Surfaces only when measuring `len(err.Error())` against a multi-MB input.

  Helpers + per-helper input classification:
  - `truncForError(s string)` — 80-char cap; for arbitrary user-controllable string default literals, JSON-Number strings, decimal RatString, enum symbols.
  - `truncBytesForError(b []byte)` — 40-char cap (sized for fixed-format diagnostic values like UUIDs and int literals); for JSON-scanner number-bytes and UUID wire bytes.
  - `truncValueForError(v any)` — `%v`-style format with type-aware fast paths (string / []byte / json.Number skip the format step); for the `%T(%v)` shape at union-default rejection sites (`walkDefault` / `encodeDefault` for unresolved unions).

  **Sweep playbook:** `grep -nE 'fmt\.Errorf\([^)]*%[qsv][^)]*\)' *.go | grep -v _test`. For each hit, classify the interpolated argument:
  1. **Schema-bounded** (`node.kind`, `f.name`, schema-defined enum symbols, fixed-format internal tokens): safe — the schema-parse step already accepted those bytes; echoing them is 1:1 with the schema input.
  2. **Wire-controlled** (wire-decoded bytes, JSON-scanner output, json.Number content, UUID wire payload, default literal from schema-parse-time validation): every such site needs a `truncForError` / `truncBytesForError` / `truncValueForError` wrap. Filing a finding requires a runnable failing test that measures `len(err.Error())` against a 1+ MiB hostile input.
  3. **Mixed** (record/map-key error wraps where the key comes from a parsed-JSON default with no upstream length cap): also needs wrapping; the schema acceptance step bounded the schema as a whole, but a giant key inside a small schema is still possible.

  Instance: ~15+ sites across coercion / UUID / enum / default-validation / decimal / special-float arms, all wrapped — the sweep grep regenerates the list; site enumeration verbatim: archive (2026-07-23 #2).

  **Stdlib-parser-error sub-pattern: errors from stdlib `json.Unmarshal`/`strconv.Atoi`/`strconv.Parse*` embed the failing input VERBATIM in their typed error structs.** No `%q` interpolation visible — but `*json.UnmarshalTypeError.Value` and `*strconv.NumError.Num` carry the full bytes; a subsequent `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", stdlibErr)` formats the message at construction (`*fmt.wrapError.Error()` returns precomputed `msg`) and caches the content. Mutating `ute.Value`/`ne.Num` via `errors.As` AFTER the `%w` wrap is too late. Two-layered defense:
  - **Length-cap at the custom `UnmarshalJSON` entry** (for `laxInt`-style types whose body wraps via `fmt.Errorf("%w", strconvErr)`): rejects before the stdlib parser builds a multi-MB error. `maxLaxIntDataLen` at `schema.go` — see `laxInt.UnmarshalJSON`.
  - **Post-hoc truncation of stdlib error structs** at the OUTERMOST wrap (for bare `*int`/`*int32` fields with no custom UnmarshalJSON): `errors.As(err, &ute)`/`errors.As(err, &ne)` mutates `ute.Value`/`ne.Num` BEFORE the final `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)`. `boundJSONErrorEcho` at `schema.go`, applied at `parse()`'s top-level json.Unmarshal wrap.

  Sweep on any json.Unmarshal: classify the target type. `string`/`bool` don't echo; `int`/`float64`/typed-numeric and custom-`UnmarshalJSON` types wrapping via `%w` both echo. Instance: 7 schema-parse fields — `aobject.Size *laxInt`, `aobject.Scale *int`, `aobject.Precision *int`, `afield.Scale *int`, `afield.Precision *int`.

  **Deferred-render sub-pattern: the trunc helper trims the RESULT, but the render that PRODUCES the result is the unbounded work.** The call site DOES wrap with a trunc helper, so the primary grep skips it as defended — but the wrapped argument is `bigRat.RatString()` / `bigRat.FloatString(scale)` / any stringify materializing the FULL value before truncation. A `5^(2^24)`-denominator `*big.Rat` took ~20 s. Fix: bound at the VALUE not the string — check magnitude (`r.Num().BitLen()`/`r.Denom().BitLen()`) and skip the render when oversized (`truncRatForError`, `ser.go`). Sweep the primary grep can't see: `grep -nE 'trunc(For|Bytes|Value)?Error\([a-zA-Z0-9_.]+\.(RatString|FloatString|String|Text|Marshal)' *.go`. Caught by FIX.md item 5's hostile-input probe TIMING THE REJECT: a megabit input rejecting in >100 ms means the cost is pre-truncation even though `len(err.Error())` is small. Instance: `buildBigDecimalPayload`, `ratToUnscaled`, `setDecimalRat`, big-decimal JSON decode all did `truncForError(r.RatString())`.

  **Why a separate entry from pattern 14b:** 14b's framing is "safety-helper bypass" focused on helpers gating acceptance/rejection (`v.SetString`/`v.SetInt`). The trunc helpers gate a *message-construction* operation that doesn't change acceptance. Without this entry the next round re-derives "error messages aren't behavior" and skips the sweep.

### AUDIT_CORE.md §Known cross-cutting policies — the json.Number bullet, verbatim before compression

- **json.Number** is a cross-cutting policy area. The deliberate design:
  - **The Avro schema is the contract.** For numeric schemas (int/long/float/double, including logical-type variants like date / timestamp-* / time-*), json.Number carries the raw numeric wire value as a JSON-number-valid string — logical-type formatting is bypassed for json.Number targets so the round-trip preserves numeric content. **json.Number is numeric-only: it is rejected for stringy schemas (string/bytes/fixed/enum) on BOTH encode and decode** — it is a numeric carrier (RFC 8259), so a text/binary target is a type mismatch (use a Go string or []byte there). The reject lives in one shared encode guard (`rejectJSONNumberRawTarget`, mirroring `appendAvroString`'s string-schema reject) and one shared decode guard (`rejectJSONNumberStringTarget`). Map keys are the one content-aware exception: validated per-key on both sides (encode and decode) so `map[json.Number]V` round-trips when all keys are valid JSON numbers — because Avro map keys are strings whose json.Number form must itself be numeric.
  - **json.Number's content must always be a valid JSON number literal.** Per the type's stdlib contract: `json.Marshal(json.Number(x))` rejects any underlying string that isn't a valid RFC 8259 number. Decode rejects when the wire content has no valid JSON-number representation (non-finite floats, arbitrary text from stringy wires that doesn't parse, non-numeric map keys); encode rejects when json.Number's source content doesn't parse as the schema's numeric type or doesn't satisfy the map-key invariant.

  Required entries to read and quote before any json.Number change (titles are stable; grep by these exact strings):
  - doc.go: `Encoding from JSON input` section.
  - BUG_AUDIT.md §Known intentional divergences:
    - `Whole-number floats encode against int / long schemas`
    - `Encode into float / double is lossy by destination`
    - `json.Number content is validated against the schema's contract`
  - In-test: `TestRegression_JSONNumberTargetRejectedForStringLikeWire` (decode reject, all stringy), `TestRegression_JSONNumberStringSourceRejectedOnEncode` (encode reject, all stringy incl bytes/fixed), `TestRegression_JSONNumberMapKeyRejected`, `TestJSONNumberMapKeyContentValidated`, `TestLogicalNumericTargetJSONNumberWritesRawWire`, `TestInvariant_EncodeDecodeTargetParity` (executable encode/decode parity matrix), `TestRegression_UnionDispatchMatrix` (the hex-json.Number case now rejects: numeric-only, no branch accepts it), `TestRegression_JSONNumberNonNumericRejectedForTemporalEncode` (encode reject on date/timestamp-*/local-timestamp-* for a json.Number whose content is a valid RFC3339/DateOnly STRING but not a number — the string-convenience arm must exclude json.Number, mirroring decode's `formatToStringKindTarget`), `TestMatrix_JSONNumberLogicalMatchesNumericTwin` (differential: a logical-on-numeric's json.Number encode verdict must equal its underlying int/long twin's, across every encode context — the numeric-carrier exclusion is uniform across every string-Kind encode gate, §14c).

### AUDIT_CORE.md §Audit conventions 2 and 5, verbatim before compression

2. **Every claimed bug requires a runnable Go test verified failing against the codebase as it currently sits on disk.** Verification means: a sandbox module (typically `/tmp/avro_audit_verify/`) that imports `github.com/twmb/avro`, the test file go-vetted, `go test -run TestRegression_<name>` run, and the failure output observed and quoted in the report. A test written without running is not a confirmed finding. The current git branch is irrelevant — what matters is that the test fails against the source on disk.

   This applies **per site, not per bug shape**. Multiple sites with the same shape each need their own failing test. Phrases like "the same shape applies for defense in depth" without a failing test for that specific site are not findings — those sites might have compensating downstream guards. Either write the failing test (and it becomes a real finding) or drop the site. (Instance: an auditor flagged two siblings as "defense in depth"; both were already protected by an unrelated downstream check, and the speculative fix had to be reverted.)

   **Sibling sweep is required, not optional.** After confirming a finding at site X, grep for the same shape (the dispatch arm, the stdlib call, the accumulator form) across the rest of the codebase. Either (a) confirm a second site fails with its own runnable test (now N findings, not 1), or (b) state explicitly which sites were grepped and why they are not affected — name the compensating guard or structural reason. "Only looked at site X" is incomplete. (Instances: the array zero-byte cap drift affected 4 sites, 2 buggy + 2 correct; the `big.Rat.SetString` DoS affected 4 sites across decode + encode.) Audit-time grep is much cheaper than a separate round.

   **Callback-firing claims need a value-TRANSFORMING callback.** An identity/value-preserving CustomType callback cannot distinguish "the callback fired" from "the raw value was coerced into the target" — the values coincide, so the probe passes either way. (Instance: an identity custom "confirmed" a union-branch custom fires for concrete typed targets on bare-JSON decode; a ×10 transform showed binary=70 vs JSON=7 — the custom was being skipped and plain coercion produced the same number.) Any "this callback runs/is suppressed here" probe must use a callback whose output is distinguishable from its input — a marker recording `%T`/`%v`, or an arithmetic transform.


5. **Source comments, commit messages, AND public-API doc strings in twmb/avro are not authoritative evidence.** Comments like "matches Java's X" or "unreachable: ..." are claims the maintainer made when the comment was written; they may have rotted, been wrong from the start, or describe an outdated state. Same for commit messages — a recent commit saying "all four dispatch sites agree" is a claim about what the patch achieves, not proof. **Public-API doc strings are testable contracts**, not free-form description: "Root preserves all metadata including doc strings, namespaces, and custom properties" makes a value-preservation claim that needs testing at boundaries (precision-edge ints, large strings, unusual unicode) — reading the doc as truth instead of as a claim is how the precision-loss bug at `Schema.Root` survived. When a finding turns on whether a comment's/message's/doc-string's claim is true, verification goes against the cited source (`apache/avro` / `fastavro` / `hamba/avro`, or — for in-repo claims — the actual implementation). Specifically: a parity comment, a branch marked "unreachable", a TestRegression name, a commit message "mirrors helper X", a doc-string "preserves all metadata" — each is a claim to verify against the cited source (list the helper's documented input shapes and test each; probe doc'd value-preservation at precision edges), never evidence by itself. (Instances: (i) the union-default coercion comment claimed Java parity but three reference impls disagreed; (ii) a fix's message said `serNull` was brought "into parity" with `isNilValue` but only Interface peeling was added, not Pointer — `&nilPtr` still rejected; (iii) `Schema.Root`'s doc promised "preserves all metadata" while two `json.Unmarshal`-into-any sites silently rounded ints > 2^53.) Comments/messages/doc strings are starting points for intent; the source code (here and at the cited reference) is what's true.

### AUDIT_CORE.md §Findings that don't count, verbatim before compression

## Findings that don't count

Reminder: the §"Before changing behavior — required pre-action gate" section is the imperative form. Run it before proposing anything. The bullets here describe what gets rejected after the fact — but the work to *avoid* the rejection is the pre-action gate.

These submissions don't qualify as findings:

- **"This area looks suspicious"** — without a concrete failing test, it's not a bug.
- **"Could be more efficient"** — perf regressions count only with benchstat showing the regression.
- **"This doesn't match the spec letter"** — where Java and fastavro agree on the implementation behavior even on spec-ambiguous points, the implementation IS the spec for interop purposes; what's deployed is the contract.
- **"Convenience" form for spec-defined output** — the spec sometimes mandates non-intuitive output (e.g. decimal-on-bytes JSON encoding as a codepoint-mapped string `"!"` rather than a number `0.33`). "It would be more readable to emit a number" is not a finding — that's a deliberate spec violation, the kind the audit targets in the REVERSE direction (places that emit the convenience form when Java/spec mandates the structural form).
- **Re-finding something already pinned by a `TestRegression_*` test** — UNLESS the pin is itself the bug (pattern 13). The grep `TestRegression_` is the pre-report check; with 110+ regression tests already pinning specific bugs, the not-a-finding case is common. The exception is pattern 12: a pinned rejection that violates round-trip parity IS the finding (quote the pin and propose its replacement).
- **Re-litigating documented intentional behavior** — *this is what the §"Before changing behavior" pre-action gate exists to prevent.* If the gate's verdict is "documented as intentional," the change does not qualify regardless of how clean the asymmetry-fix looks. A genuine policy challenge requires concrete new evidence (deployed Java/fastavro producer that emits data twmb can't read, real-world user reporting wire-format divergence) that the documented rationale doesn't address — surfaced as a Suspected/Finding asking the user whether to revisit, not as a unilateral code change. Conformance-test pins with comments containing `"Documenting"`, `"Intentional"`, `"Asymmetry: X (intentional)"`, `"Pre-fix this …; post-fix the two are now uniform"`, or names referencing §"Known intentional divergences" are the in-test form of documented intentional. Same treatment.
- **Encode/decode "asymmetry → fix" reflex on json.Number for documented-lenient cases.** The json.Number schema-contract design and the whole-number-float / lossy-by-destination leniencies are documented policy -- the canonical statement (with the required entries to quote) is the "Known cross-cutting policies" list inside the pre-action gate above. Proposed changes there must quote the named entries and bring new evidence.
- **Tests that don't compile.** `go vet` is the gate; drafts that fail it are not submittable.
- **Symptom fix that introduces a new asymmetry.** Relaxing a strict check so one input passes changes behavior for every input it deliberately rejected (instance: `parseUUID` fall-through accepted 16-char non-UUIDs, breaking binary↔JSON parity). Root-cause fixes beat local relaxations.

### NOT_BUGS.md — tombstoned entries whose bodies had never actually been tombstoned, verbatim before compression to the one-line form


#### NOT_BUGS #44

44. **(tombstone, fully netted) Union-branch selection matches named types (record/enum/fixed) by UNQUALIFIED short-name across namespaces — deliberately siding with fastavro over the stricter Java.** `findMatchingBranch` / `kindsMatchTier` (compat.go) rank branches full-name > unqualified-name > promotion, and the unqualified tier covers all three named kinds; fixed still requires equal `size`, folded into the union predicate per spec. Java's soft match is RECORD-ONLY (Resolver.java:632-664, whose own comment admits it disagrees with the spec); fastavro matches twmb. It reuses the same lenient `namesMatch` tier direct same-kind resolution uses, where Java IS lenient, so direct and union resolution stay internally consistent. Do NOT "fix" toward Java's record-only rule. Nets: the evolution + promotion matrices' union-widen/narrow rows with the fastavro differential arm. Re-opens: a new branch-ranking tier, or a Java release adopting the spec rule. Verbatim: BUG_AUDIT.md §Distillation archive (2026-07-27).

   **Fixed SIZE is folded INTO the union match predicate (`kindsMatchTier`), per spec + fastavro.** The spec's union match predicate is "both schemas are fixed whose sizes and (unqualified) names match", and selection takes "the first schema in the reader's union that matches" (`_index.md` 691, 717) — size is part of MATCHING, not a post-selection check. A same-name `fixed` of a different `size` returns `matchNone`, so `findMatchingBranch` skips it and continues to a later size-matching branch, order-independently, for Resolve AND CheckCompatibility, on both wires. fastavro does the same (`match_schemas` → None, `read_union` skips-and-continues, `_read_py.py`); Java returns on the full-name match and then fails on size (`Resolver.firstMatchingBranch`), the 1.8.x soft-match whose own comment admits the spec divergence — twmb previously shared it and now follows spec + fastavro per cross-impl rules 2+3 (relaxed, safe: a reorder-decodable value, no corruption). The direct (non-union) fixed path still validates size via `checkSameKind` / `doResolve`. Pinned by `TestRegression_UnionFixedSizeFoldedIntoSelection`; probed against the spec, `Resolver.java`, and fastavro 1.12.2 (source + execution).

#### NOT_BUGS #45

45. **(tombstone, fully netted) `WithMaxDecompressedBlockBytes` is enforced UP FRONT and uniformly via the `BoundedDecompressor` capability.** `Reader.readBlock` type-asserts the codec and calls `DecompressBounded(compressed, max)`, refusing an over-cap block BEFORE allocating it; all four built-ins implement it (null/snappy declared-length pre-check, deflate `io.LimitReader(max+1)`, zstd lazily building with `zstd.WithDecoderMaxMemory(max)`), so a codec SUPPLIED via `WithCodec` — including a `NopCloser`-wrapped or user-built zstd instance — is bounded exactly like a name-resolved one. The only unbounded case is a custom codec that does not implement the capability: honestly unbounded, with no post-decompression backstop (false comfort once allocated); the count bound and trailing-bytes check use the RETURNED slice's real length, so there is no arithmetic hazard. Do NOT re-file "a supplied zstd instance ignores `WithMaxDecompressedBlockBytes`" — it does not. Nets: `TestRegression_OCFUserBuiltinCodecBoundsDecompression`, `TestRegression_OCFSuppliedZstdInstanceBounded`, `TestRegression_OCFCustomCodecBoundedDecompressorContract`, `TestMatrix_CodecDecompressReturnShapes` (alias/nil/short/pad/error return shapes). Re-opens: a new built-in codec, or a proposal to add a post-decompression re-check. Verbatim: BUG_AUDIT.md §Distillation archive (2026-07-25 #3).

#### NOT_BUGS #47

47. **(tombstone, fully netted) The binary decoder rejects a WIDTH-OVERFLOW varint** — one whose FINAL byte carries value-bits beyond the type width (int 5th byte > `0x0f`, long 10th byte > `0x01`) — with "uvarint/uvarlong overflows N bits"; a legal-width non-canonical (overlong) form that keeps every value-bit inside the width (`0x80 0x00` = 0) IS accepted. twmb is liberal on encoding WIDTH and strict only on bits that overflow it. Java masks the surplus bits and accepts, but the three references disagree on the resulting value and every accept is silently-wrong (`FF FF FF FF 7F` against `"int"`: Java −2147483648, goavro −17179869184, fastavro out of int32 range entirely) — cross-implementation policy rule 1 governs. No conformant encoder emits the form, and twmb never produces what it rejects, so there is no encode/decode route divergence. Distinct from #4 (the JSON decoder's legal-WIDTH union-index leniency). Do NOT "fix" to mask like Java. Nets: `varint_overflow`/`varlong_overflow` (deser_test.go), `overlong-count` (matrix_framing_test.go, `putZigzagOverlong`), the reader-grammar census. Re-opens: a real foreign producer emitting the form, or a new varint reader outside `readUvarint`/`readUvarlong`. Verbatim: BUG_AUDIT.md §Distillation archive (2026-07-25 #3).

  **(a) EXCLUSIVITY.** A container kind carrying ANOTHER kind's defining key hard-rejects (`invalid <kind> has schema for other types`) — keep-strict; Java (props) and fastavro (executed accepts) diverge. The reject is the cache/metadata walkers' kind-keyed-child-scope soundness premise.

  **(b) SHAPE-CONDITIONAL ROUTING** on a kind that does not bind the key: a schema-shaped stray body surfaces structurally as-written as its ONLY surface (render dedup skips stray-reached names; survival is props-independent); a malformed body rides in Props verbatim as its ONLY surface, structural field ZERO. capture⟺verdict: the metadata captures run the parser's own decodes (`stringSliceFrom`/`decodeLaxInt`), so structural-field-set ⟺ parse-consumed.

  **(c) A WRAPPED REFERENCE** rejects schema-shaped structural keys ("unknown complex type"); non-structural/malformed extras merge onto the spliced def as props, def-wins exact-key (Java drops usage-site extras; fastavro rejects the spelling — executed).

  **(d)** SchemaFor's walkers pass unbound structural keys through untouched, verdict-parity with Parse. **(e)** The binding-kind gate is `walkNodeChildren`'s DEFAULT; only the metadata walker opts into stray enumeration (pinned asymmetry). **(f)** Exact-case only (#46): stray routing is placement-conditional, never case-conditional.

  **(g) BARE-EMISSION losslessness.** Clause (b)'s "as-written is its ONLY surface" holds through `Root().Schema()`. The render collapses a node to its bare type name only when it carries NOTHING beyond `Type` — asked once as `nodeCarriesOnlyType` (schema_node.go), DERIVED from SchemaNode's field set. Two sites ask it (`toJSONWalk`'s primitive arm and its name-reference arm); each previously held its own hand-written list and both were missing members, so a stray `symbols`/`size`/`aliases`/`doc`/`name` on a primitive survived `String()` and `Root()` and was silently dropped by the rebuild. `Branches` is the ONE classified exemption — no JSON key routes to it outside a union, so a hand-built value elsewhere is inert (`TestRegression_NonUnionBranchesInertInRebuild`). The durable guard is `TestInvariant_BareEmissionCoversEverySchemaNodeField`, which sets every exported field in turn and requires the predicate to notice, so a field added later FAILS until someone classifies it.

  **(h) Losslessness is a CONJUNCTION, and (g) proved only half of it.** A guard requiring the shortcut to BLOCK says nothing about whether the longer form it falls through to EMITS — which `EnumDefault` did not. The guard is now a ROUND TRIP: set, emit, re-parse, read the value back off the metadata FIELDS (never the rendered text, whose key ORDER made an earlier survival check report losses that had not happened). Every exported field carries one of three classifications, checked in both directions: EXEMPT (`Branches` off a union, `EnumDefault` without its carrier — no emitted form, so it must NOT block), RELOCATED (`Precision`/`Scale`, and `HasEnumDefault` since clause (j): the emitted key rides to Props on a carrier that does not bind it, #71), or ROUND-TRIPPING on its own field. There is deliberately NO fourth "dropped by policy" class, so a field that emits a key the re-parse discards fails here instead of being classified as an accepted loss.

  **(i) The SIBLING predicate on the same walk.** `nodeIsNameRefShape` — whether a stamped reference may be replaced by the definition it names — was the other hand-written list, of eight fields, silently discarding the seven it did not name on an extracted-then-EDITED node. It is now derived through the same walk, `nodeCarriesNothingBut`, with an exemption set that is EXACTLY the adjudicated usage-site attributes: `Doc`/`Aliases`/`Namespace`/`LogicalType` per #25 (a definition cannot carry a second name, namespace or doc for its usage site, and the parse LANDS those four on the structural fields, so deriving without them would convert #25's adjudicated silent drop into a hard "unknown complex type" on the extraction feature), plus `Props`, which clause (c) MERGES. `Precision`/`Scale` are NOT exempt: the parse routes an unconsumed pair to Props, so a non-zero value on those FIELDS can only be a caller's direct write. Registered as census **Q17**, which runs the metadata splice and the CACHE splice over one corpus and requires the same verdict per wrapper key.

  **(j) A reserved key that is neither BOUND nor SURFACEABLE has Props as its only surface — the type-level `default` and `order` (maintainer-RULED 2026-07-27, reversing the drop clause (h) had recorded as policy).** Both are FIELD attributes; at the type level only an enum binds `"default"` (#54) and NO kind binds `"order"`, and neither has a SchemaNode field of its own on a kind that does not bind it — so both were captured by the reserved-key set and then dropped, reaching neither a structural field nor Props. That violates the biconditional the family drives (structural field set IFF consumed, Props = raw minus consumed, never both and never neither) and is the same class as (g)'s bare-emission loss. Both references PRESERVE where the kind does not bind: Java's `SCHEMA_RESERVED` (Schema.java:175-176) omits both and `ENUM_RESERVED` (:178-180) adds `default` alone, applied at :1857/:1880/:1940/:1950/:1963 vs :1928 for enum; fastavro 1.12.2 keeps both on every kind (EXECUTED, 28 cells). Cross-impl rule 2 agrees, and this is PRESERVATION, not an accept/reject loosening. **#46 is REFINED, not reversed:** it governs CASE VARIANTS and presumes the exact spelling is CONSUMED; where the kind does not bind there is no capture, so its premise is absent, and `"Default"`/`"Order"` stay ordinary props everywhere including the kind whose exact spelling binds. **SCOPE is type-level only:** Java's `FIELD_RESERVED` (:503-504) binds both at the FIELD level and so does twmb, so a record field's `default`/`order` stay consumed into `SchemaField.Default`/`.Order` and must never reach `SchemaField.Props`. The routing is DERIVED, not enumerated: `schemaReservedKeyForObject` asks `schemaKeyBinds` and keeps a key out of Props for exactly two reasons — the kind BINDS it, or the kind SURFACES it as-written on a structural field (`canonicalStrayKey` plus a shape-OK body). Consumed-ness still wins at a splice: an enum definition swallows a wrapper's `"default"` rather than carrying a second one. The one member of the reserved set that is BOUND on every kind yet still reaches neither surface is `doc` with a non-string body — a deliberate Java-parity exception, ruled separately as #72.
