### AUDIT_PATTERNS.md §Structural blind spots — the six largest entries, verbatim before compression


#### - **Dual type-name namespaces (normalized internal vs preser

- **Dual type-name namespaces (normalized internal vs preserved-as-written public-API).** `node.kind` is normalized by the builder (`"error"`→`"record"` at `case "record", "error":`); `SchemaNode.Type` preserves the JSON-as-written name. Wire helpers dispatch on the internal field (canonical case only); metadata helpers mirroring them dispatch on the public field and need the alias set listed explicitly. Invisible to: "find every site that calls this helper" sweeps (the helper IS the site — its case list missed an alias), "find every site dispatching on the same field" (wire parallel dispatches on a DIFFERENT field), and encode/decode-parity (wire agrees via upstream normalization). Probe: for every metadata-helper fix dispatching on a preserved field, enumerate the normalizer's collapse set; concentrate the predicate in one helper (`isRecordKind`). Known dual-namespace pairs: `aobject.Type` ↔ `schemaNode.kind`; `SchemaNode.Type` ↔ `schemaNode.kind`. Instance: `coerceMetadataDefault`/`branchAcceptsDefault`/`lookupNameRef` triple in `schema_node.go` missing `"error"` alongside `"record"` while wire parallels (`coerceDefault`/`validateDefault`/`walkDefault`) were correct via builder collapse.

    - **Per-value predicate drift between dual-namespace helpers** (broader than alias-set drift). Paired helpers implementing the SAME conceptual contract in different namespaces (`*schemaNode` internal vs `*SchemaNode` public) can diverge on the per-value predicates, not just type-name aliases. The wire helper does full value validation (range/whole-number/codepoint/size checks); the metadata helper is type-only (`case string, []byte: return true`). Probe: when a wire-side validator is updated, grep the metadata-side namespace (`*SchemaNode`) for parallel helpers; if a parallel exists and doesn't call the updated wire validator, file as `[sibling-of-fix]`. Fix: extend the wire helper to accept metadata-side normalized types, then delegate. Instance: `branchAcceptsDefault` numeric/bytes arms accepted on type only while `validateDefault` (via `defaultAsInt32`/`defaultAsInt64`/`defaultAsFloat`, `validateAvroByteString`+size-check) applied range/precision/codepoint/size predicates.

    - **Within-helper arm asymmetry: when one arm of a multi-arm dispatch helper is updated to apply a wire-side predicate, every OTHER arm in the same switch is a candidate.** The grep `grep -n '<helper-name>' *.go` finds the helper but not its arms; the angle is "for each `case`, does this arm need a wire-side predicate the analogous wire arm enforces?" Numeric/bytes cases delegate easily (standalone `defaultAsInt32`/`defaultAsFloat`); structural cases (record/error, array, map) look self-contained (`_, ok := val.(map[string]any); return ok`) but the wire side validates per-element via a recursive walker (`walkDefault` calling `validateLeaf`). Fix: mirror the wire recursion locally.

    - **The mandatory artifact: an exhaustive wire-vs-metadata per-arm table.** "Verified per-arm" verbally is the trap. The probe: for every `case`, write a one-line row naming the kind, wire predicate, metadata predicate, and whether they agree. If the metadata side lumps via `case A, B:`, EACH LUMPED KIND IS A SEPARATE ROW. The disagreeing row is the bug.

    - **Combined `case A, B:` clauses are a specific hiding pattern.** When metadata writes `case "string", "enum":` and wire writes separate cases with different per-value predicates, the combined body applies whichever predicate is correct for ONE kind to all. Grep: `grep -nE 'case "[a-z]+", "[a-z]+"' <helper-file>` enumerates combined cases; for each ask "do the wire equivalents share this body, or does ONE have a per-kind predicate the body doesn't apply?" If yes, split the case.

    - **Concrete instances:**
        - Round N: structural arms of `branchAcceptsDefault` were type-only (`_, ok := val.(map[string]any); return ok`); a union `[{record needing X}, {record needing nothing}]` default `{}` metadata-matched the first branch while wire picked the second → `Root().Fields[0].Default["shared"]` came back `float64(42)` vs wire-decoded `int64(42)`. Fix: mirror wire recursion locally.
        - Round N (post-fix re-audit): `branchAcceptsDefault`'s `case "string", "enum":` combined — body only checked `val.(string)`, but wire enum arm needs `slices.Contains(node.symbols, sym)`. Union `[enum:{A,B}, bytes]` default `"Z"` metadata-matched enum, wire picked bytes → `Default[u]=string("Z")` vs wire `[]byte("Z")`. Fix: split `case "enum":` with `slices.Contains(t.Symbols, sym)` (guarded by `len(t.Symbols) > 0`).

    The angle generalizes: any helper pattern-matching on a public field with N cases where a fix updated K < N (especially combined `case A, B:` clauses) owes a per-arm audit of the remaining N-K. The probe is the table.

#### - **The completeness critic — a net's held-CONSTANT axes are

- **The completeness critic — a net's held-CONSTANT axes are its blind spots, and the vacuity neuter cannot see them.** The neuter asks "is the arm this net exercises actually asserted?" (break the production line; confirm the net reds). It is BLIND to an input class the net never exercises — there is no arm to neuter for an axis the rows hold constant. The complementary, mandatory check after writing or extending any net: **list the axes the net holds CONSTANT, then ask whether the production code VARIES each.** A varied-in-code, constant-in-net axis is an unexercised input class — a hole no neuter can surface. Probe: enumerate the net's fixed choices — target freshness (always-fresh `reflect.New` vs a reused/pre-populated target), the option cube (`TaggedUnions`/`TagLogicalTypes`/`LinkedinFloats` left default), the value's position/ambiguity (distinct-type vs overlapping-same-Go-type union; null-first vs null-second; scalar vs container element), the dispatch branch (matched custom vs all-skip; `Decode==nil` vs callback), the logical-suppression mode (wildcard non-suppressing vs LogicalType-matching suppressing) — and for each fixed choice name the code path it forecloses. A foreclosed path the code reaches under a different choice is the missing cell; add it, THEN neuter its new arm. The critic runs at NET-DESIGN time; the neuter runs after, on each arm the (now-complete) net exercises. Instance: `custom_skip_decode_test` held four axes constant (fresh targets, no `TaggedUnions`, distinct-type unions, wildcard customs) and each hid a real all-skip divergence — target-map reuse, tagged-into-interface, overlapping-branch ordinal, logical suppression — none of which the neuter could have surfaced because the rows never reached those arms. Second instance: `TestRegression_ResolvedDecodeJSONMatchesBinary` held the INPUT-FORM axis constant (only twmb's own bare `EncodeJSON` output) and its one union cell had no colliding branches, so the tagged `{"branch": value}` envelope — the only form Java's JsonEncoder and fastavro emit — never reached `decodeJSONResolved`, whose untagged intermediate silently rewrote tagged branch identity via first-match re-encode (and the decoded VALUE, where writer→reader resolution differed per branch); closed by the input-form × collision-shape × resolution matrix `TestMatrix_ResolvedJSONUnionInputForms` + `TestDifferentialFastavroResolvedJSONUnion`.

- *(tombstone -- netted)* **Two-mechanism recursion-depth accounting must charge each schema edge once on BOTH mechanisms** (encode threads a depth parameter; decode bumps stateful sl.depth on node entry; the invariant breaks at multi-entry seams -- fast-body dispatch, *Via re-entry, null-union optimizers, array-element unions). Netted: the depth-uniformity oracle suite -- TestDepthUniformityOracle / TestDepthUniformityMutual (hand-assembled wire, every recursive shape x every path, ONE trip depth), TestDepthUniformityNestedStructRecord, TestDepthBoundCyclicContainers. Re-opens if a fix touches any depth+1 / sl.depth++ / depth >= maxDepth site (sweep ser/deser/unsafe/json_codec/json_decode/resolve/skip.go, classify sole-entry vs dispatch-hop) or a new recursive shape / entry seam lands outside the oracle's shape list. Full entry: BUG_AUDIT.md, Distillation archive (2026-07-14; earlier history 2026-07-01).

- *(tombstone -- netted)* **A bounded recursive walk that serializes a tree has FOUR independent cost axes** -- structural depth, per-node value-payload depth (must mirror json.Marshal's FULL recursion), DAG expansion (one node-count budget shared across the WHOLE walk), and nested serializations threading the SAME budget pointer, never a fresh one. Netted: TestRegression_SchemaNodeSchemaDeepValueBounded / SchemaNodeWalkDepthAllChannels / SchemaNodeSharedDAGExpansionBounded / SchemaNodeDuplicateNamedDefinitionBounded (fixes boundedSerializableValue/valueNestsTooDeep, maxSchemaJSONNodes + valueWalkLimit, toJSONShared -- schema_node.go). Re-opens if a new recursive walk serializes user-reachable trees or a nested marshal/re-walk inside a budgeted walk allocates a fresh budget. Full entry: BUG_AUDIT.md, Distillation archive (2026-07-14; earlier history 2026-07-01).

#### - **Lenient walker skips a nil child that its strict sibling

- **Lenient walker skips a nil child that its strict sibling dereferences.** A family of walkers over the same node tree (`walkDefault` driving `validateDefault`/`convertDefaultBytes` vs `encodeDefault`) must agree on nil-child handling. Lenient walkers guard `node == nil`/`child != nil` and SKIP (validating vacuously); the strict walker derefs `node.kind` unguarded → nil-panic at `Parse` on a transiently-nil forward-ref child. Invisible to lenient-walker tests (pass vacuously) and wire round-trip tests (panic at parse, before encode). Probe: for any tree-walk family, list which walkers guard nil children and which deref unguarded — the asymmetry IS the bug; fix is usually ordering (wire all children before the strict walk), not a nil-guard. Four escalating sub-shapes (full narrative: BUG_AUDIT.md §Distillation archive (2026-07-21)): (1) forward-ref array-items/map-values/nested-record defaults panicked in `encodeDefault` while `validateDefault` skipped — fixed by deferring resolution+encode to a two-phase finalize; (2) **dual-representation**: forward-ref UNION branches left `node.branches[i]` nil because the fixup patched only the wire fn tables (`m.ser.fns[idx]`), never the structure node — a fixup must update EVERY representation (`branches[idx] = nt.node`); (3) **name-derived artifacts captured at parse time** (dup-detection key, TaggedUnions `branchNames`/`logicalNames`, tagged-map `ser.branchNames`) held the unresolved name — `finalizeUnionNames` re-derives from resolved nodes; (4) **non-nil-but-INCOMPLETE in-construction node** hid a recursion bound — `nodeAwaitsForwardRef`'s `b.building` check defers its defaults, and the relocated `encodeDefault` needs the wire codec's `maxDepth` (`encodeDefaultDepth`) to reject infinite defaults. Meta-lesson: a deferral that moves an encode from a PARTIAL node to a COMPLETE one can expose recursion the partiality silently bounded — re-probe the relocated encoder against an infinite-default schema. General rule: enumerate every name-derived artifact a build site computes and either compute it from the resolved node or re-derive it in finalize.

- *(tombstone -- netted, once re-opened)* **A non-wire path re-derives a resolution the parser already computed -- and must reproduce it EXACTLY, including position-dependence AND the binding grammar's kind-gating** -- or consume the binding directly. Class net: the FEATURE x WALKER parity harness (matrix_feature_walker_test.go; adding a feature or walker = adding a ROW/DRIVER, never a hardcoded expectation) + TestMatrix_CacheKeylessDefCollection / TestMatrix_LeadingDotNameNormalization / TestMatrix_CacheStrayStructuralKey; four instance families (positional splice, keyless carve-out, leading-dot #62, stray-key def store #63) fixed and neuter-proven. Root lesson of the 2026-07-19 re-open: a gating sweep's true scope is the shared enumerator's CALLER SET, never the file. The walkNodeChildren caller table (keep current when adding a caller): collectTreeDefs GATED, inlineNodeChildren GATED, nodeFromJSONObject strayKeys-by-design (pinned TestRegression_MetadataStrayKeySurfacedAsWritten); own-kind-gate siblings: dedupNamedTypes / pinCustomSchemaScope / normalizeSchemaScope / addTypeAliases (schema_for), collectNamedTypes (schema_node); un-gated by design: coerceTreeDefaults (registration-free), toJSONWalk's emitter (kind-gated emission). Re-opens if a new walker / name-resolution rule / feature spelling lands without its harness row or driver, a parser resolution gains a dimension the twins don't cross, or a new walkNodeChildren caller (or same-contract enumerator under another name) lands without a caller-table row. Full entry + re-open narrative: archive (2026-07-14, 2026-07-19); this entry's pre-compression text: archive (2026-07-24 #8).

#### - **Error messages echo unbounded user-controllable input — 

- **Error messages echo unbounded user-controllable input — log / RPC / metric-label amplification.** Distinct from P9 (parser-CPU) and P16 (precision-fix DoS): the parser rejects in O(1) via a length cap, BUT the rejection message interpolates the input verbatim. A 10 MiB hostile json.Number → a 10 MiB error message → 1:1 amplification through logging, RPC error channels, Prometheus labels, tracing. Invisible to timing probes (~0.1 ms), to wire-correctness probes (the error is correct, just enormous), and to unit tests that assert an error EXISTS. Surfaces only when measuring `len(err.Error())` against a multi-MB input.

  Helpers: `truncForError(string)` 80-char cap (arbitrary user strings, JSON-Number strings, decimal RatString, enum symbols) · `truncBytesForError([]byte)` 40-char cap (JSON-scanner number bytes, UUID wire bytes) · `truncValueForError(any)` `%v` with type-aware fast paths (the `%T(%v)` union-default rejection shape).

  **Sweep playbook:** `grep -nE 'fmt\.Errorf\([^)]*%[qsv][^)]*\)' *.go | grep -v _test`, then classify the interpolated argument: (1) SCHEMA-BOUNDED (`node.kind`, `f.name`, declared enum symbols) — safe, the parse already accepted those bytes; (2) WIRE-CONTROLLED (decoded bytes, JSON-scanner output, json.Number content, UUID payload, a default literal from parse-time validation) — needs a trunc wrap, and a finding needs a runnable test measuring `len(err.Error())` against a 1+ MiB input; (3) MIXED (record/map-key wraps where the key comes from a parsed default with no upstream cap) — also needs wrapping, since a giant key can sit inside a small schema. ~15+ wrapped sites; enumeration verbatim: archive (2026-07-23 #2, 2026-07-27 #4).

  **Stdlib-parser-error sub-pattern: stdlib errors embed the failing input VERBATIM in their typed structs**, with no `%q` for the grep to see — `*json.UnmarshalTypeError.Value` and `*strconv.NumError.Num` carry the full bytes, and a later `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` formats and CACHES the message at construction, so mutating the struct after the wrap is too late. Two-layered defense: a length cap at the custom `UnmarshalJSON` entry (`maxLaxIntDataLen`, `laxInt.UnmarshalJSON`) for types that wrap a strconv error, and post-hoc truncation via `errors.As` at the OUTERMOST wrap (`boundJSONErrorEcho`, applied at `parse()`'s top-level json.Unmarshal) for bare `*int`/`*int32` fields with no custom unmarshaler. Sweep any json.Unmarshal by TARGET TYPE: `string`/`bool` don't echo; `int`/`float64`/typed-numeric and custom-`UnmarshalJSON`-wrapping-`%w` types both do. Instance: 7 schema-parse fields (`aobject.Size`, `.Scale`, `.Precision`, `afield.Scale`, `.Precision`).

  **Deferred-render sub-pattern: the trunc helper trims the RESULT, but the render that PRODUCES it is the unbounded work.** The call site DOES wrap, so the primary grep skips it as defended — but the wrapped argument is `bigRat.RatString()` / `FloatString(scale)` / any stringify that materializes the FULL value before truncation (a `5^(2^24)`-denominator `*big.Rat` took ~20 s). Fix at the VALUE, not the string: check `BitLen()` and skip the render when oversized (`truncRatForError`, ser.go). Second grep, which the primary cannot see: `grep -nE 'trunc(For|Bytes|Value)?Error\([a-zA-Z0-9_.]+\.(RatString|FloatString|String|Text|Marshal)' *.go`. Caught by FIX.md item 5's hostile-input probe TIMING the reject: a megabit input rejecting in >100 ms means the cost is pre-truncation even though `len(err.Error())` is small.

  **Why separate from P14b:** 14b is about helpers gating ACCEPTANCE; the trunc helpers gate MESSAGE CONSTRUCTION, which changes no verdict. Without this entry the next round re-derives "error messages aren't behavior" and skips the sweep.

#### - **`SchemaFor` (Go-type → schema) has no wire-format counte

- **`SchemaFor` (Go-type → schema) has no wire-format counterpart, so the wire-parity and four-axis lenses never reach it — now netted generatively by `TestSchemaForEncodeParity` (schema_for_test.go).** `SchemaFor` is a pure Go-reflection→schema-JSON transform; its contract is "every valid Go type produces a valid, round-trippable, internally-consistent schema with uniform accept/reject strictness." The **build-accepts/encode-rejects sub-class** is the highest-yield shape and sits where every other net is blind: (a) mutation testing finds weak ASSERTIONS over exercised paths, never a MISSING input class (no AST node for an absent json.Number case); (b) the combinatorial matrix is schema→value, never Go-type→schema; (c) Java/fastavro have no SchemaFor to differential against; (d) `SchemaFor[T]` is compile-time generic, so a byte-fuzzer can't synthesize field types. The durable net: because `schema_for_test.go` is `package avro` (internal), it mirrors SchemaFor's body (`inferRecord`→`dedupNamedTypes`→Marshal→Parse) over a `reflect.StructOf`-built struct and asserts **SchemaFor-accepts ⟹ Encode-accepts**. Two construction rules: (1) cross every codec-special-cased / Kind-misleading Go type (`json.Number`, `time.Time`, `time.Duration`, `big.Rat`, byte containers) plus aliases/pointers/slices/maps/nesting; (2) drive a NON-EMPTY recursive sample value (`sampleValue`), not the zero value — a nil pointer / empty slice / map never materializes its leaf type. Meta-lesson: mutation testing measures the net's assertion quality, not input enumeration — a missing-input-class bug needs a generative input axis, reflect-driven for SchemaFor. Instance: `inferType`'s `reflect.String` arm emitted `"string"` for `json.Number` but the codec rejects `json.Number` for stringy schemas; fixed by an exact-type `case jsonNumberType:` reject (after the CustomType loop). Pinned by `TestSchemaForRejectsJSONNumber` + `TestSchemaForEncodeParity`. Other Go-type sub-shapes:
  - **Memoization keyed coarser than the value it caches.** `seen map[reflect.Type]string` cached one name per Go type, but a `[N]byte`'s name depends on `(type, logical)` — `"uuid"` when tagged, `t.Name()` plain. Same type used both ways → dangling reference. Rule: audit every memoization (`seen`, name tables, wiring maps) — "is the key as fine-grained as everything that varies the output?"
  - **A generic pre-tokenizer over-applies to a take-the-rest field.** `splitTag`'s bracket-balance scan ran over the whole tag including a `default=` value documented to take the rest verbatim, rejecting a default with an unbalanced `(`/`[`. Rule: when one option's grammar is "the literal remainder," the tokenizer's structural checks must stop at that boundary.
  - **Asymmetric strictness: validates one compatibility axis, silently defers another.** `SchemaFor` rejected Go-type/logical-tag mismatches at build time but let a `default=` that fits the Avro type yet overflows the narrower Go field through. Rule: when a builder validates axis A up-front, axis B (same question, different value source) should validate up-front too. Instance: `inferType` (schema_for.go) inferred `"string"` for a non-string type implementing only one text direction (TextMarshaler XOR TextUnmarshaler) → a one-directional schema; now refused at build (962f7b6).

#### - **Vacuous nets — a net runs the path but cannot SEE a wron

- **Vacuous nets — a net runs the path but cannot SEE a wrong result (green even with the production arm it nominally covers broken).** The audit's nets are themselves audit territory: a green net proves nothing if no defect could red it. Four sub-shapes: (1) **any-target dodge** — decodes into `any`/`[]any`/`map[string]any` (all assignable) where the bug class is typed placement / type-strictness; the typed setter arms never run. (2) **short-circuit dodge** — the row's target is resolved by an earlier fast path (exactly-assignable / `setCustomResult` pointer-walk / interface) so the arm under test is dead code under the row (the canonical case: a `*int32` union row resolved before the union branches arm — shape (r)). (3) **weak assertion** — asserts only success / no-error / a count / mutual-agreement between two SAME-path decodes, never value/bytes vs an INDEPENDENT oracle. (4) **round-trip-same-type dodge** — encode T → decode the same concrete T (or encode-only, never decode back), so cross-target placement arms never run. **Probe (the whole point — never claim a net is live without it): neuter the production arm the net nominally covers (Edit-reverse) and run JUST that net.** Green-under-defect = vacuous → strengthen (cross a typed/named target so no fast-path short-circuits; assert value/bytes vs an independent oracle, not mutual agreement) and re-confirm it now reds. A "strengthened" row that still stays green under the neuter is the same dead-cell mistake. **Critical neuter-targeting trap: neuter the EXACT arm the row uses, not a sibling** — a typed `[]int32` decode uses the NATIVE loop (`deserNativeArrayIntLoop`), NOT the set-closure fallback (`deserArrayIntLoop`), and the `any` arm uses the IFACE loop (`deserArrayIntIfaceLoop`); neutering the wrong one leaves the row green and falsely "proves" liveness. **Not every weak-looking net is a finding:** re-encode-stability (`encode(decode(wire))==wire`) IS a real value oracle for value-CHANGING decode bugs (it reds under a `+1` neuter for injective-encode types) — vacuous only for the narrow non-injective class (time-of-day date-drop, ±0.0, json.Number normalization, enum-ordinal aliasing); a mutual-agreement-vs-self-reference net (concurrency) is the right oracle for its race-detection charter; and a vacuous cell whose arm is covered by a sibling net (custom-skip typed placement → `custom_skip_decode_test`; `*T` decode → NullUnionNilEquivalence/PointerIndirection; value correctness → the differential matrices) is local hygiene, not a unique gap. Probe: for every `var x any`/`map[string]any` decode target, every `if err != nil`-only / `len()==N`-only / count-only assertion, and every encode-then-decode-same-type, ask "what production line can I break that keeps this green?" — then break it. Instances: `TestMatrix_ReflectUnsafePathParity` (decoded both wires, asserted only no-error — fixed to assert the unsafe-decoded value); `TestMatrix_CustomTypes`/count (all-skip into `any` + count-only); the shape-(r) `*int32` union cell; `TestMatrix_ForeignContainerFraming` typed-slice arms (`len`-only over the native block-walker, value-blind across foreign framings); `TestMatrix_AliasEvolution` (resolved decode asserted err-only, never the reader-shaped value).

#### NOT_BUGS #63

63. **(tombstone, fully netted) The stray-structural-key family (maintainer-adjudicated 2026-07-14; clauses through 2026-07-27).** Per-clause narrative — how each was found, what the blast-radius measurement showed, which driver defect a neuter caught — is archived (2026-07-23 #4; 2026-07-27 #2, #3, #4); every clause below keeps its ruling and its pin.

  **(a) EXCLUSIVITY.** A container kind carrying ANOTHER kind's defining key hard-rejects (`invalid <kind> has schema for other types`) — keep-strict; Java (props) and fastavro (executed accepts) diverge. The reject is the cache/metadata walkers' kind-keyed-child-scope soundness premise.

  **(b) SHAPE-CONDITIONAL ROUTING** on a kind that does not bind the key: a schema-shaped stray body surfaces structurally as-written as its ONLY surface (render dedup skips stray-reached names; survival is props-independent); a malformed body rides in Props verbatim as its ONLY surface, structural field ZERO. capture⟺verdict: the metadata captures run the parser's own decodes (`stringSliceFrom`/`decodeLaxInt`), so structural-field-set ⟺ parse-consumed.

  **(c) A WRAPPED REFERENCE** rejects schema-shaped structural keys ("unknown complex type"); non-structural/malformed extras merge onto the spliced def as props, def-wins exact-key (Java drops usage-site extras; fastavro rejects the spelling — executed).

  **(d)** SchemaFor's walkers pass unbound structural keys through untouched, verdict-parity with Parse. **(e)** The binding-kind gate is `walkNodeChildren`'s DEFAULT; only the metadata walker opts into stray enumeration (pinned asymmetry). **(f)** Exact-case only (#46): stray routing is placement-conditional, never case-conditional.

  **(g)/(h) BARE-EMISSION losslessness, which is a CONJUNCTION.** Clause (b)'s "as-written is its ONLY surface" holds through `Root().Schema()`. The render collapses a node to its bare type name only when it carries NOTHING beyond `Type`, asked once as `nodeCarriesOnlyType` (schema_node.go), DERIVED from SchemaNode's field set; two sites ask it (`toJSONWalk`'s primitive and name-reference arms), each previously holding its own hand-written list, both missing members. A guard requiring the shortcut to BLOCK proves only half — it says nothing about whether the longer form it falls through to EMITS, which `EnumDefault` did not. The guard `TestInvariant_BareEmissionCoversEverySchemaNodeField` is therefore a ROUND TRIP: set every exported field in turn, emit, re-parse, read the value back off the metadata FIELDS (never the rendered text, whose key ORDER made an earlier survival check report losses that had not happened). Every field carries one of three classifications, checked both directions: EXEMPT (`Branches` off a union — no JSON key routes to it, `TestRegression_NonUnionBranchesInertInRebuild`; `EnumDefault` without its carrier), RELOCATED (`Precision`/`Scale`/`HasEnumDefault` — the emitted key rides to Props on a carrier that does not bind it, #71), or ROUND-TRIPPING on its own field. There is deliberately NO fourth "dropped by policy" class, so a field emitting a key the re-parse discards FAILS here instead of being classified as an accepted loss, and a field added later fails until someone classifies it.

  **(i) The SIBLING predicate on the same walk.** `nodeIsNameRefShape` — may a stamped reference be replaced by the definition it names — was the other hand-written list, of eight fields, silently discarding the seven it did not name on an extracted-then-EDITED node. It is now derived through the same walk, `nodeCarriesNothingBut`, exempting EXACTLY the adjudicated usage-site attributes: `Doc`/`Aliases`/`Namespace`/`LogicalType` per #25 (deriving without them would turn #25's adjudicated silent drop into a hard "unknown complex type" on the extraction feature), plus `Props`, which clause (c) MERGES. `Precision`/`Scale` are NOT exempt: the parse routes an unconsumed pair to Props, so a non-zero value on those FIELDS can only be a caller's direct write. Census **Q17**.

  **(j) A reserved key that is neither BOUND nor SURFACEABLE has Props as its only surface — the type-level `default` and `order` (maintainer-RULED 2026-07-27, reversing the drop clause (h) had recorded as policy).** Both are FIELD attributes: at the type level only an enum binds `"default"` (#54) and NO kind binds `"order"`, so on a non-binding kind neither has a SchemaNode field to land on, and both were captured by the reserved-key set and then dropped — violating the biconditional the family drives, in the same class as (g)'s loss. Both references PRESERVE where the kind does not bind: Java's `SCHEMA_RESERVED` (Schema.java:175-176) omits both and `ENUM_RESERVED` (:178-180) adds `default` alone (applied :1857/:1880/:1940/:1950/:1963 vs :1928 for enum); fastavro 1.12.2 keeps both on every kind (EXECUTED, 28 cells). PRESERVATION, not an accept/reject loosening; cross-impl rule 2 agrees. **#46 is REFINED, not reversed:** it governs CASE VARIANTS and presumes the exact spelling is CONSUMED, so where the kind does not bind its premise is absent and `"Default"`/`"Order"` stay ordinary props everywhere. **SCOPE is type-level only:** Java's `FIELD_RESERVED` (:503-504) binds both at the FIELD level and so does twmb, so a record field's `default`/`order` stay consumed and must never reach `SchemaField.Props`. The routing is DERIVED: `schemaReservedKeyForObject` asks `schemaKeyBinds` and keeps a key out of Props for exactly two reasons — the kind BINDS it, or the kind SURFACES it as-written on a structural field (`canonicalStrayKey` plus a shape-OK body). Consumed-ness still wins at a splice. The one reserved key BOUND on every kind that still reaches neither surface is `doc` with a non-string body (#72). A body the shape check cannot READ AT ALL — an explicit JSON null — is #73: malformed, so Props-verbatim here and reject where the kind binds.

  **Nets:** `TestMatrix_ReservedAttributeEnumeration` is the COMPLETENESS question for this family — every reserved attribute × body shape × level × kind, expectations derived per cell from the references — and the per-ruling pins are what each clause owns: the 360-cell stray-key matrix · `TestMatrix_StrayBodyShapeRouting` · the strayPS placement matrices · `TestMatrix_SpliceWrapperReservedKeyMerge` · the FEATURE × WALKER rows · `TestInvariant_BareEmissionCoversEverySchemaNodeField` (+ `_CoversPresenceOnlyFields`, #74) · `_NameRefSpliceCoversEverySchemaNodeField` · `_NodeFieldRuleTablesNameRealFields` · `TestMatrix_CallerComposedAndEditedNodes` (204 cells over recursive, diamond, forward-reference and cache-cross-parse structures) · `TestMatrix_TypeLevelBindingRouting` · `TestRegression_TypeLevelDefaultOrderSurviveTheRebuild` · `_FieldLevelDefaultOrderStayConsumed` · `TestMatrix_ReservedKeyBodyPresence` (#73) · `TestDifferentialFastavroTypeLevelBindingRouting` · census Q4/Q16/Q17/Q18. **Re-opens:** a new walker/consult of either tree representation without its R1 row, or a new reserved-key read/shape check not shared with the parser's decodes. **OPEN under this family:** a structural key written as its destination's ZERO at a stray placement reaches neither surface today — 63 cells the enumeration records as UNRULED, since neither reference can adjudicate a question about a metadata tree they do not have.

#### NOT_BUGS #33

33. **Field-level `logicalType` annotation on unions is lifted onto the first non-null branch.** Schemas like `{"name":"ts","type":["null","long"],"logicalType":"timestamp-millis"}` (AVRO-2015/AVRO-3014 common user error) parse with `timestamp-millis` applied to the `long` branch, so encode/decode of `time.Time` work directly. Apache Avro detects + warns but doesn't lift (Schema.java:1871-1877); fastavro/hamba/goavro preserve it as a field property only. Twmb-unique among Go impls; wire identical (raw long varint). Edge `["null","string","long"]`+`timestamp-millis`: the lift targets `string`, `validateLogical` detects the mismatch and soft-drops (`o.Logical = ""`) — matches the references (no logical effective). The metadata API does NOT reflect the lift (`Root().Fields[0].Type.LogicalType` empty; it surfaces in `Field.Props["logicalType"]`) — also matching all references.
    **Spelling-agnostic clause (2026-07-25):** "first non-null branch" means the first branch that is not the null TYPE, in either spelling the grammar admits — bare `"null"` and wrapped `{"type":"null"}` (with or without props / a logicalType, both inert on a null) are the same branch. The skip previously matched only the bare form, so under `[{"type":"null"},"long"]` the annotation landed ON the null branch and a `time.Time` no longer encoded. Every as-written null-branch decision now routes through the one `aschema.isNullBranch` predicate (P20).
    **Parameters-fill clause (ruled 2026-07-26).** The ANNOTATION and its PARAMETERS are separate questions. Closer-to-the-type wins the ANNOTATION: a target declaring its own `logicalType` keeps it and the field's is dropped. The field still completes MISSING precision/scale, but only where the EFFECTIVE logical (the target's own if it has one, else the field's) is `"decimal"` — routed through `liftEffectiveLogical`, the same predicate the consume verdict reads, so navigation, landing and parameter completion cannot disagree. Before this the object arm completed parameters and the union arm did not, so `{"type":"bytes","logicalType":"decimal"}` under a field carrying `precision`/`scale` BUILT while its `["null",{same}]` twin REJECTED — the same post-lift schema, a spelling-dependent verdict. No reference has an opinion, so INTERNAL CONSISTENCY governs, cross-impl rule 2 breaking the tie toward accepting. The gate's side effect (parameters no longer copied onto a non-decimal effective target) is unobservable, MEASURED: canonical form and wire identical with the pair present, absent, and at scale 0 vs 2. See `liftFieldLogicalIntoType`/`liftTarget`/`liftEffectiveLogical` (schema.go); pinned by `TestRegression_FieldLogicalLiftSpellingParity`, `_FieldParamsOnNonDecimalTargetAreUnobservable`, census Q5. Consume-verdict landing rules: #71.

   The lift is a per-problem-shape concession, NOT "make every buggy schema work." Supported shapes — `["null","T"]` and its object-form null twin (one shape per the spelling clause), `"T"`, `{"type":"T"}`, each with a field-level logical and no own annotation — were each added for a specific deployed-buggy/interop need. INTENTIONALLY unsupported: a lift onto a NON-FIRST non-null branch (`["null","string","long"]`+`timestamp-millis` targets the `string` and soft-drops rather than searching for a fitting branch). A repeated null branch is not an unsupported shape but a rejected schema (the duplicate-union-type check fires before any lift). The bar for adding a shape is a real-world producer breakage — surface as Suspected with evidence and ask.

#### NOT_BUGS #54

54. **Enum FIELD-default symbol membership is validated at schema parse — deliberately stricter than every reference; keep-strict (maintainer-adjudicated).** Java's parse-time field-default validation accepts ANY textual value for an enum-typed field default: `isValidDefault` groups ENUM with STRING/BYTES/FIXED and checks only `isTextual()` (Schema.java:1755-1759); symbol containment is enforced only for the enum-LEVEL `"default"` in EnumSchema's constructor (:1100). fastavro 1.12.2 parses a non-member enum field default outright (executed). twmb validates at parse because a non-member field default can never encode — accepting it just moves the failure from parse (fail-fast, actionable) to first default-fill encode. The same check is what lets union default coercion pick a later branch instead of mis-selecting the enum on a non-member string (`TestRegression_UnionDefaultMetadataMatchesWireBranch_EnumArm`). Cross-impl rule 1 decided keep-strict; do NOT re-file it as an interop divergence.
    **Enum-LEVEL non-string/null defaults: twmb's reject is fastavro-CORROBORATED, not twmb-stricter.** `"default":3` and `"default":null` both reject in twmb and in fastavro 1.12.2 (`Default value for enum must be in symbols list`, executed, both shapes). Only Java ignores them — it reads the enum-level default through `getOptionalText`, which returns null for a non-text node, so the :1100 containment check is skipped and the malformed default silently drops. Two-of-three reject; the Java-only silent drop is the same anti-silent-drop shape as #55. (That lenient `textValue()` read is Java's general mechanism for its reserved TEXT attributes, and where twmb FOLLOWS it instead of rejecting, the case is #72's `doc`.)
    **Closing clause (2026-07-24): the reject is decided by TOKEN TYPE, not by membership-on-the-Unmarshal-zero-value** — the shape #73 later generalized to every typed body read. The old membership-only check let the ignored `json.Unmarshal` error's `""` (and null's no-op) flow into the symbol test, so under a `WithLaxNames` fn accepting empty name components a schema whose symbols legitimately include `""` ACCEPTED `"default":5`/`null` and silently BOUND the `""` symbol — resolution filled it for unknown writer symbols while `Root().HasEnumDefault` reported false (wire↔metadata split). Post-fix: a non-string token — number, bool, array, object, explicit null — hard-rejects `enum default <token> is not a string` (bounded echo) in BOTH strict and lax modes, BEFORE membership; `"default":""` stays legal exactly when `""` is a member. Pins: `TestRegression_EnumDefaultLaxPhantomBindRejected`/`_ExplicitNullRejected`/`_NonStringEchoNamesToken`, boundary `TestEnumDefaultEmptySymbolBoundary`, matrices `TestMatrix_EnumDefaultTokenClassElimination` + `_EnumFieldDefaultTokenTypes` + `TestRegression_EnumRefWrapperDefaultInert`, differential `TestDifferentialFastavroEnumDefaultToken` (calibrated: fastavro TYPE-checks field defaults but not membership; rejects the wrapped-ref shape outright).

#### NOT_BUGS #48

48. **When a CustomType is registered and every decoder returns `ErrSkipCustomType` at a node, the decoder RE-DECODES the wire into the target through the base deserializer — byte-identical to a no-custom decode. For a wildcard custom (empty `LogicalType` AND `AvroType`, the documented "property-based dispatch like Kafka Connect types" form) that matches LEAF nodes but SKIPS container nodes, decoding into a deeply-nested TYPED Go target (struct / `[]T` / `map[string]T`) re-decodes each container's subtree once per enclosing level → O(depth²), bounded by `maxDepth`. The common property-dispatch target — decoding into `any` / `map[string]any` — is O(n) single-pass. This is the ACCEPTED, bounded cost of faithful re-decode, not a bug.** When all decoders skip at a node, `wrapDeserWithCustomDecoders` (custom_type.go) / `wrapDecodeJSONWithCustomDecoders` (json_decode.go) re-decode the original wire into the real target rather than placing the probe-decoded `any` value — re-decode is what makes a REUSED map keep its existing keys, a logical node land in a base typed target, and an overlapping union recover its exact wire branch, none of which placing the `any` reproduces. A no-match fast path (`sl.bypassCustom`) keeps the common case a single O(subtree) pass; it fires only when NO custom matched anywhere in the subtree, so a wildcard that matches leaves (every level's `customMatches` changes) re-decodes with customs active at each container level along a typed spine → O(depth²). The earlier O(value) converter (`assignCanonical`) was REMOVED because it diverged from a no-custom decode on map-reuse / `TaggedUnions` / logical-into-base-target; re-decode is correct on all three, and the worst case is bounded by `maxDepth`. To decode untrusted deeply-nested data through a wildcard property-dispatch custom, target `any` / `map[string]any` (single-pass) or register the custom against a specific `LogicalType`/`AvroType` (no wrapper installs on container nodes). Encode is unaffected (it transforms then serializes once — no re-encode). Documented on `CustomType.Decode` (custom_type.go). Correctness pinned by `TestRegression_CustomSkipDecodeMatchesNoCustom` (custom_skip_decode_test.go); the O(depth²) cost is the deliberate trade-off. Do NOT re-file "wildcard custom decode into a typed target is slow / O(depth²)" as a DoS.

#### NOT_BUGS #61

61. **A contract-violating `encoding.TextAppender` is guarded only where its misbehavior is DETECTABLE: binary encode rejects a shorter-than-input return with a named error; everything else is documented trust (maintainer-adjudicated: minimal guard).** `appendAvroString`'s inline-write slow path reserves a 1-byte length placeholder, lets the user's `AppendText(dst)` write into the buffer, and backfills the header from the returned slice's length — so that slice is trusted arithmetic input. The guard (`len(dst) < mark+hdrLen` → `SemanticError`, "AppendText returned a slice shorter than its input") converts the previously-PANICKING shape (a fresh short return like `return []byte(s), nil`: slice-bounds panic at every position where accumulated output exceeds the return, silent empty string at top level) into a named error. Two residuals are DELIBERATE: (a) a fresh return >= the input length passes the check and silently replaces all previously-encoded output (err == nil, typically an undecodable wire) — detecting it would cost a per-string memcmp of everything encoded so far, a hot-path tax rejected for the caller's own contract violation; (b) the JSON encoder materializes text via `AppendText(nil)` (`textValue`), so fresh returns are taken verbatim — nothing to guard, and for violating appenders the two wires legitimately differ. Reference posture EXECUTED (go1.26.2, GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2): Go's own `encoding/json/v2` PANICS identically on the same appender (`slice bounds out of range [33:1]` in `jsontext.(*encoderState).AppendRaw`), so the trusting posture is the stdlib norm and twmb's guard is strictly more defensive; json v1 never calls `AppendText`, and decode-side `TextUnmarshaler` is immune. Do NOT extend the guard to prefix-compare, and do NOT re-file the silent shapes or the binary↔JSON violator divergence. Pinned by `TestRegression_AppendTextShortReturnNamedError` and `TestMatrix_AppendTextReturnShapes` / `_JSONImmunity` (return shape × position, exact observed bytes for the undetectable shapes, plain-string-twin byte identity for legal appends; neuter-verified — disabling the guard reproduces the recovered panics at record/struct/array/map positions, the silent `x`-wire at union, and the pin's `[11:1]` panic, while every legal/silent/JSON cell stays green).

#### NOT_BUGS #10

10. **String-form float defaults at single-field outer type only (`{"type":"float","default":"1.5"}`)** are accepted at parse and materialize as `float32(1.5)` / `float64(2.718)`. Java parity with `parseField`'s text→DoubleNode coercion at `Schema.java:1899-1902` — fires only when the OUTER `fieldSchema.getType()` is FLOAT or DOUBLE. avro-rs's `resolve_float`/`resolve_double` (types.rs:960-986) reject regular numeric strings but accept IEEE 754 special tokens; twmb's `parseFloatAcceptOverflow` accepts both. Per Avro 1.12 §"Record" the JSON-string form is technically invalid; the Java coercion is preserved for interop. **A DIRECT scalar float/double UNION branch does NOT coerce a string default** — `["double"]` default `"5"` rejects at parse and `["double","string"]` default `"5"` picks the string branch — matching Java's `isValidDefault` UNION arm, avro-rs, and goavro (`defaultAsFloat` has no string arm; the scalar union leaf is not coerced). **But a float/double field NESTED inside a record/array/map DOES coerce, even when that container is a union branch** — `[{record{x:double}}, {record{x:string}}]` default `{"x":"5"}` coerces `"5"`→`float64(5)` and selects the double-record branch. This is a deliberate leniency BEYOND Java (Java's `parseField` coercion is outer-field-only, so Java rejects the nested string-numeric and picks the string-record branch; twmb leans permissive per cross-impl rule 2). The wire selector (`validateLeaf`→`coerceDefault` per child, schema.go) and the metadata selector (`branchAcceptsDefault`→`coerceMetadataDefault`, schema_node.go) apply the SAME coercion, so `Root().Default` reports the same branch the wire auto-fill decodes on both binary and JSON — NO metadata↔wire divergence. Do NOT re-file "twmb coerces nested string-double defaults, Java doesn't" or propose removing the nested coercion; revisit only on a real interop breakage with evidence. See `defaultAsFloat`'s strict body + the nested-`float32` arm at schema.go, `coerceDefault`'s doc, `TestParseFloatDefaultFromString`, `TestRegression_UnionDefaultStringMatchesOnlyStringAcceptingBranches` (scalar-union reject), and `TestRegression_UnionContainerNestedFloatDefaultSelectionMatchesWire` (nested-container coercion, wire==metadata).

#### NOT_BUGS #56

56. **Flat-format (goavro-style) fields surface POST-LIFT in the metadata API (maintainer-adjudicated).** A field written as a bare string complex-kind type with the kind's defining key alongside the field's own keys (`{"name":"E","type":"enum","symbols":[...]}`) is a deliberate parse-input concession to linkedin/goavro's flat field format; the wire parser lifts the defining keys into a nested type definition named after the field (`liftFlatFieldType`, schema_parse.go). `Root()` describes that same post-lift schema: the type node carries the name and defining content, the routed keys (defining key, doc, logicalType/precision/scale, custom props; name/namespace for named kinds) do NOT appear in `SchemaField.Props`, and `Root().Schema()` rebuilds the nested form. Rationale: the as-written flat shape is unrepresentable through the rebuild (`toJSONWalk` emits a SchemaNode as a nested type OBJECT, and the lift gate fires only on a bare STRING type, so a Props-carrying posture cannot round-trip), and no reference posture exists because both references reject the flat form outright — fastavro 1.12.2 raises `UnknownType` (executed), and Java resolves a textual field type as a NAME (Schema.java:1828-1829; the complex-kind dispatch at :1830-1844 applies only to object nodes), so `"enum"` is an undefined name there. Deliberately DIFFERENT from #33's Props-carrying posture: the logicalType lift's as-written shape IS preserved by the rebuild and re-lifts on re-parse, so Props-carrying round-trips there. The lift decision and key routing are shared helpers (`flatFieldNeedsLift` / `flatLiftTypeMap`) used by both the wire parser and the metadata walker, so the two cannot drift. Pinned by `TestRegression_FlatFieldRootSchemaRoundTrip`, `_FlatFixedNameRefDefaultCoerced`, and the `TestMatrix_FlatFieldLift*` suite (kind × namespace × logicals × name-ref-default shapes × no-lift boundary parity × degenerate content; neuter-verified — gating the metadata twin off reproduces the empty-node / rebuild-error / uncoerced-default shapes on every lift-dependent cell while the no-lift parity cells stay green). Verdict parity (#71): malformed precision/scale in the flat spelling take the TYPE-level consumed gate's verdict, so flat and nested twins agree on every body shape (`TestRegression_FlatFieldMalformedPrecisionMatchesNestedTwin`).

## Distillation archive (2026-07-28 #9) — NOT_BUGS #68, verbatim

Compressed to the standard tombstone form during the NOT_BUGS size pass, the
first taken after the file's ~120KB cap was written into AUDIT_CORE's size
guard (it had been enforced from memory for many rounds). The entry is fully
netted, so what it keeps in NOT_BUGS is the ruling, the nets and the re-open
condition; the budget-derivation detail lives here.

68. **(tombstone, fully netted) SchemaFor renders `CustomType.Schema` through the ERROR-REPORTING walk and composes a PRIVATE COPY.** The bare walk's truncate-to-nil posture belongs to error-LESS surfaces; SchemaFor has an error channel, so an over-budget or cyclic custom schema FAILS the build with the walk's named error rather than silently parsing as a null prop, and never mutates caller-owned SchemaNode storage (the boundary deep-copies). **Budgets are measured against what `json.Marshal` will EMIT, not the value's Go shape** — three escapes closed: a value's own `MarshalJSON`/`MarshalText` (`marshalEmitLen`, Marshaler first, matching json.Marshal's order; an erroring method left uncharged so the marshal names its own failure); a non-string map key (`mapKeyEmitLen`, mirroring `encoding/json`'s `resolveKeyName` ARM FOR ARM INCLUDING ITS GUARDS, its terminal panic arm becoming `valueWalkBadMapKey`); and ESCAPED length (a control byte costs six output bytes; 64 MiB had admitted 402,628,629). Charging is EXACT, by a NON-ALLOCATING counting scan with EARLY EXIT — exactness keeps ASCII billing at 1x instead of a 6x worst case rejecting ordinary schemas at a sixth of the cap. **The P21 restatement licence is CONDITIONAL and is the re-open condition.** Nets: `TestCensus_Q9_EscapedLenMatchesEmitterOverEveryByte` (+ `_OnMultiByte`, `_Codepoint…`; expectations derived from the package's own emitter over all 256 bytes, multi-byte runes, invalid UTF-8, U+2028/9, the HTML trio — `SetEscapeHTML(false)` reds them) · `_EscapedLenScanIsBoundedByTheLimit` · `TestRegression_WalkBudgetMapKeyMatchesJSONKeyResolver` (12 key shapes vs `json.Marshal` EXECUTED) · `_WalkBudgetChargesEveryEmissionRoute` · `_KeepsMarshalOpaqueValuesOpaque` · `_MeasurementIsItselfBounded` · `_SchemaForOverBudgetCustomSchemaErrors` · `_CustomSchemaBudgetAxes` · `_SchemaForLeavesCallerSchemaStorageUnmutated` · the caller-storage snapshot in every `TestMatrix_SchemaForCustomSchemaScope` cell. Re-opens: a NEW emission route json.Marshal takes that the walk does not charge, or a new boundary marshalling caller values without the canonicalizing copy. Verbatim: archive (2026-07-27; 2026-07-27 #5).

## Distillation archive (2026-07-28 #15) — NOT_BUGS #74, verbatim

Compressed to tombstone form during the NOT_BUGS pass the cap-table round's
own writes mandated. Fully netted by the reserved-attribute enumeration; what
the live entry keeps is the ruling, the per-attribute conditions the gate must
quote, and the net.

74. **An attribute WRITTEN AS ITS DESTINATION'S ZERO is written, and the emission condition that decides its fate is PER ATTRIBUTE — copied from Apache Avro's emitters, not generalized from one of them (maintainer-RULED 2026-07-27).** `doc:""` survives on the four named kinds and on a record field; `logicalType:""` survives on every kind; `order:""` REJECTS; `aliases:[]` and a `doc:""` on a primitive or container keep being dropped. The four answers come from four different Apache Avro sites, and a blanket "was it written" mechanism would have shipped a divergence at two of them.
    **Why the value alone cannot answer it.** An attribute read into a plain `string`/`int` has no present/absent companion, so `x != ""` means both "the caller chose a value" and "the caller chose the value that is my zero": a VALIDATOR guarded that way skips exactly the zero (`order:""` parsed while every other non-spec order rejected), an EMITTER drops it (`doc:""`/`logicalType:""` died in the rebuild). Distinct from #73, a body the decode cannot READ: this one decodes perfectly into a value indistinguishable from absence, so no body check can see it.
    **Java, source-derived per site (apache/avro:main, JVM-less here so every rule carries its line):** doc emits when NON-NULL — `if (getDoc() != null)` at Schema.java:1039 (record), :1154 (enum), :1367 (fixed) and :1062 (field) — and `parseDoc`→`getOptionalText` (:1997, :2041) returns `""` unchanged, so an empty doc is a doc. `aliases` emits when NON-EMPTY (`aliases == null || aliases.isEmpty()` :886; `f.aliases != null && !f.aliases.isEmpty()` :1070), so an empty list is dropped. `order` is decided on the NODE (`if (orderNode != null) Order.valueOf(...)` :1895-1897), so `""` reaches valueOf and throws. `logicalType` is absent from SCHEMA_RESERVED (:175-176), so `parseProperties` (:1983) keeps it as an ordinary property whatever its content. **fastavro 1.12.2 preserves all four verbatim (executed), so the two drops below are Java-siding, recorded as such rather than left looking like oversights.**
    **PLACEMENT AUTHORITY decides a cell no single reference can, and it is the rule the rest of this entry rests on: the authority for a placement is whichever reference actually HAS that placement, and it governs the empty and the non-empty body ALIKE.** Apache Avro has no doc slot on a primitive or a container — `parseDoc` is called from `parseRecord`/`parseEnum`/`parseFixed`/`parseField` and nowhere else — so it does not drop a doc there, it has no opinion there; fastavro has the placement and preserves. This package already followed fastavro at that placement for a non-empty doc, so `{"type":"int","doc":""}` is PRESERVED too (ruled 2026-07-28, correcting an earlier ruling that read Apache Avro's ABSENCE as a drop while its non-empty sibling followed fastavro's PRESENCE — one placement cannot answer to two authorities). `logicalType` rides on every kind for the same reason.
    **Where NEITHER reference has the placement, this package's own adjudicated posture governs** — the same basis #33 and #71 rest on. A structural key written as its destination's ZERO on a kind that does not bind it (`name:""`, `namespace:""`, `aliases:[]`, `symbols:[]`, `size:0`, `fields:[]`) reached NEITHER surface: consumed out of Props because the body is shape-OK, then dropped by the rebuild because the value is the zero. Apache Avro skips every stray key as reserved and keeps none; fastavro keeps every stray key and drops none; neither is answering a question about a metadata tree. #63(b) is: as-written is the key's ONLY surface. So presence decides at the stray placement while the BINDING placement keeps its reference-derived condition — which is why `aliases:[]` still drops on a record (Apache Avro's own condition there is non-EMPTY) and survives on an int (no condition to follow).
    **The trap in preserving an empty body:** the exclusivity rule (#63(a)) is decided on the VALUE, so `symbols:["A"]` on an array rejects while `symbols:[]` is accepted. Preserving the empty one therefore emits a schema whose own re-parse has to be CHECKED — `TestRegression_StrayZeroBodySurvivesTheRebuild` asserts the emitted form's round trip per cell, and a neuter that makes the emitter write a readable body where the parse accepted an empty one reds exactly the two cells where a kind binds another defining key.
    **Presence is HIDDEN state (`docSet`/`logicalSet` on SchemaNode, `docSet` on SchemaField, `orderSet` on the parse-side field), never a new exported field.** It is registered in the hidden-state census with the proof it cannot beat a caller: unlike `refTarget`, which selects a DEFINITION, a presence flag decides only whether an attribute whose value IS the field's zero gets written, so for every value a caller sets the value that comes back is the value they set — pinned by `TestInvariant_PresenceStateIsValueTransparent` over both an extracted node (flags set) and a hand-composed twin (flags clear), with the wire, canonical form and fingerprint asserted identical across the pair.
    **The trap.** `nodeCarriesNothingBut` asks `IsZero`, so an empty doc reads as an empty node and the bare-emission shortcut collapses it BEFORE the emitter is consulted — teaching only the emitter changes nothing. The walk now asks `nodePresenceSet` for the same fields, keyed by field NAME so it composes with the exemption sets (at a splice, Doc and LogicalType are exempt usage-site attributes per #25, so presence is ignored there exactly as the value is). The guard carries an explicit REACHABILITY precondition after its first version could not red: the probe must be a node the shortcut would actually collapse.
    **Nets:** `TestMatrix_ReservedAttributeEnumeration` — the whole reserved-attribute cross product (every attribute × {absent, valid, written-zero, JSON-null, wrong-typed, quoted} × {type, field} × every kind; 2184 cells, ALL asserted, none unruled), whose expectations are DERIVED PER CELL from a cited Java source model plus executed fastavro and never from this package, with `reservedProvenance` naming what settled each family · `TestRegression_EmptyOrderRejected` (with the absent and the three legal orders as the boundary, and the case variants still rejected — #46 governs, the case-fold family stays closed) · `_EmptyDocSurvivesWhereJavaEmitsOne` (five placements, fixpoint, wire/canonical/fingerprint identical to the doc-free twin) · `_EmptyLogicalTypeSurvives` · `_EmptyAliasesStayDropped` (binding placements only, with non-empty controls so the drop is about the BODY) · `_PrimitiveDocSurvivesEitherWay` (both bodies, one authority) · `_StrayZeroBodySurvivesTheRebuild` (14 cells, each asserting the emitted form's round trip) · `_StrayReadableBodyStillRejectsOnExclusivity` (the boundary preservation must not cross) · `TestInvariant_BareEmissionCoversPresenceOnlyFields` · `_FieldPresenceOnlyDocSurvivesTheRebuild` · `_PresenceStateIsValueTransparent` · the hidden-state census. **Re-opens:** a new attribute whose zero is a legal value and whose presence nothing records, or an Apache Avro release that changes one of the four emission conditions — each is a separate cell, and the whole point of this entry is that they do not move together.

## Distillation archive (2026-07-28 #33) — the key-space round's narrative, verbatim

FULL read-only round at HEAD 4131d72. Quarantine `a6dd44e..HEAD` was one
test-only commit (371a96f, the caller-value net's absolute oracle) plus a docs
commit; the oracle's authority split — 14 values decided by an EXECUTED
`json.Marshal`, 3 by a named package rule — was re-read against the code and
nothing was owed.

**Two behavioral findings, and they are ONE SHAPE seen twice: a guard keyed in
a different space than the thing it protects.** That framing is what produced
the second finding; banking the first and moving to an unrelated front would
have left it.

Finding 1 — `compat.go:207/213`. `checkRecordFieldClaimsUnique` allocates
`claimedBy := make([]string, len(r.fields))`, stores the claiming writer-field
NAME, and reads presence off `claimedBy[ri] != ""`. A writer field named `""`
therefore claims a reader slot invisibly, and a second writer field reaching
the same slot through a reader ALIAS is not detected. `CheckCompatibility`
returns nil where `Resolve` returns a `*CompatibilityError` — precisely the
divergence the guard's own comment says it exists to prevent, and whose pin
(`conformance_test.go`, "CheckCompatibility also rejects
(CheckCompatibility/Resolve parity)") asserts the lockstep using `old_name` /
`new_name`. Order is the control: with the `""`-named writer field declared
SECOND the sentinel has already been overwritten and both APIs reject, so the
declaration order alone flips the verdict. Sibling sweep found both siblings
clean and structurally so, not accidentally: `resolve.go:312` carries a
separate `readerMatched []bool` and uses the name string only for the message;
`json_decode.go:1297` carries `seen []bool` and guards `seen[idx] &&
seenKey[idx] != key`. compat.go is the sole site that made one variable do both
jobs. Reachability is `WithLaxNames` with a caller fn that accepts `""` — a
shape the package already knows it must carry, since `internalReparseNames`
exists exactly because the library re-parses user text under an
accept-everything validator.

Finding 2 — `schema.go:2312-2315` (and its twin in `finalizeUnionNames`). The
union duplicate-branch check keys named branches by FULLNAME and unnamed ones
by KIND; the tag table is keyed by fullname AND by `kind + "." + logical`. Two
key spaces, one guard. Both halves of the mismatch are reachable:

  - Over-rejects. `[{"type":"record","name":"map",...},{"type":"map",...}]` is
    a union of two different types and is refused as `duplicate union type
    "map"`. Java refuses it too (`Schema.java:1261-1266` keys `indexByName` by
    `getFullName()`, which for an unnamed schema returns the kind string —
    source-read, no JVM available); fastavro 1.12.2 ACCEPTS all five variants
    (executed). A real reference SPLIT, but rule 1 backs the rejection: the
    Avro JSON union envelope would be ambiguous between the two branches. NOT
    filed as a finding.
  - Under-rejects, and this is the bug.
    `[{"type":"bytes","logicalType":"decimal",...},{"type":"fixed","name":"decimal","namespace":"bytes","size":4}]`
    passes the check (keys `bytes` / `bytes.decimal`) while both branches tag
    as `bytes.decimal`. `ser.branchNames[bn] = i` / `[ln] = i` are unguarded,
    so the later branch silently wins, and the decimal branch's own
    `TaggedUnions+TagLogicalTypes` JSON fails to decode against the schema that
    produced it. `string.uuid` and `int.date` are the same cell; every name
    involved is valid under the STRICT Avro regex.

The tell that made finding 2 findable: four lines below the unguarded writes,
`addUnionShortNameFallbacks` writes into the SAME map and guards it twice —
`shortCount[short] != 1` and `if _, exists := ser.branchNames[short]`. An
asymmetric arm next to a guarded one is the shape, not the absolution.

**Two of my own probes were wrong before they were right, and controls caught
both — not inspection.** (a) I predicted union-branch selection would mask a
decodable branch for array/map the way it once did for fixed SIZE; the parser
rejects a union of two arrays outright, which IS the compensating guard and is
why only the NAMED kinds needed size folded in. (b) I read `Root().Schema()` as
broken under lax names across seven cells until its own doc-string said the
original Parse's opts must be threaded through; with `lax` passed, all twelve
cells round-trip. Both were premise errors of the kind the framework's
"execute reference claims" rule exists for.

Fronts: compat/resolve lockstep (2 findings) · inverse-density by test-reference
COUNT over every exported identifier, which is what surfaced `atype` (zero
references anywhere in the repo) and `rabin` · lax-names × every surface ·
union branch selection · the OCF writer state machine. Verified: `atype`'s 31
constants each round-trip through the surface its package doc names;
`rabin.go`'s full `hash.Hash64` contract plus a table/step check against the
Java reference; twelve empty-name schemas round-trip String/Canonical/
Fingerprint and the metadata rebuild; `Writer.count` tracks buffered datums on
both the `Encode` and the `Write` path, so `Reset`/`Flush`/`Close` cannot
discard a buffered block.

Gate: finding 1's `claimedBy` was introduced in-range by `8a1efc1`, finding 2's
check key scheme by `cf91ceb` — both introduced deliberately, and in both cases
the proposed change EXTENDS the introducing commit's stated intent
(CheckCompatibility↔Resolve parity; unambiguous union branches) rather than
reversing it, so there is no ping-pong to halt on. Nothing in NOT_BUGS covers
either; #42 fixes the tag SPELLING and is what makes the collision possible,
without addressing the shared key space.

Oracles: `go test -count=1 ./...` and the fastavro differential (1.12.2, venv at
`~/.cache/avro-audit-venv` intact with cramjam + zstandard) both green, 0 skips,
no `missing optional dependency` marker. Java ABSENT — JVM-less — so every Java
claim in this round is source-read, not executed.
